measuredFidelity.note: The rig's 6.75-degree leg splay (render.leg-stance) settled ankle daylight at 48.5% against the concept's 46.9%. Round 7 then found that Junebug's SIGNATURE idle pose carried an 8-degree inward leg roll, authored when the rig ran its legs straight down, which closed the ankles to 0.325ft against the bind pose's 0.756 and failed rubric 3.12 in idle while the bind-pose render this command reads stayed correct. The same roll was in all five signature idles and was removed from all of them; an FK sweep now reads every idle within 2% of bind. Re-measured 2026-08-12 after the detector itself was rebuilt to work for the whole roster: the backdrop is now sampled per column (seven sheets are vignetted past the old tolerance), a column counts as occupied by fraction rather than by any single pixel, and the shoe's two tones are read off the concept instead of the hardcoded red/cream that was Junebug's own shoe. Her shoe deltas TIGHTENED, from +2.23/+2.93 under the old classifier to +0.43/-0.78 as tone shares (41.2/25.5 concept against 41.6/24.8 delivered); the round-7 critic note below quotes the old red/cream figures and is left as the record of what was measured then.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is right and it is right by measurement, not by eye: head 34.0% of figure height against the turnaround's 33.9% (+0.10), head width:height 0.82 against 0.84, ankle daylight 48.5 against 46.9. With colour stripped she is still unmistakably the scowling kid with a bun, a headband and a swept tail. Held off 5 by butt-joined primitives, and I re-observed all three the round-7 critic named, each cropped at 4-10x from the region I cite. (1) BUN/CROWN SHELF, junebug-front-review.png x 220-330 y 55-115: the bun sits on the crown ring with a hard vertical step at BOTH silhouette edges and a shadow line across its base — no fillet, a visible corner, dead centre in the front view. (2) HEADBAND STUB, junebug-profile-review.png x 285-370 y 55-165 at 10x over a magenta backdrop: the band's rear end is a flat-cut rectangle terminating in silhouette against true background, where the concept sweeps it behind the ear to the nape. (3) PONYTAIL TIP, x 290-520 y 40-310: the tail tube ends on a flat circular cut and a separate smaller blob is stuck onto it, the seam a full crease ring with a notch either side, against a concept tip that tapers to a drawn arrowhead. A fourth: the pelvis is a flat-bottomed slab that overhangs the thigh tubes with a hard horizontal ledge across the whole hip, visible on the front board at 4x (x 180-360 y 370-420) and on both profile boards. Nothing is severed — a connected-component pass over all four boards returns exactly one component each.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Child proportion is exact and measured, not asserted: head height delta +0.10 points, head aspect -0.02, ankle daylight +1.61 — every 6b metric inside tolerance, and the head:body read is the turnaround's, never the proxy's. The A-pose boards hold the drawn stance with the arms down and daylight between the thighs and calves, so 3.12 passes on the board and again in the run still. The second clause of the 4 bar — 'joints read as connected forms' — is where it stops. The pelvis-to-thigh is the offender: build_leg's top ring simply terminates at 1.72ft inside a separately built seat, so at 4x on both the front and profile boards you see a slab overhanging a narrower tube with a lip, not a hip. The knee is nearly formless too — the ring table runs 0.180 at the knee against 0.172 just above it, a 5% swell that renders as a straight tapering cylinder in profile. It stays a 4 because the joints that carry motion hold: the run still shows a round deltoid under the sleeve cap, a continuous elbow line and a knee that bends without tearing, and the jersey hem covers the pelvis ledge at every gameplay camera.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The one category below the floor, and the deciding clause is the 4 bar's own words: 'one designed mass'. What ships is four stacked primitives with five visible joins. MEASURED first. Default band (5-45% of head height) reads 1.38 minima/row against the concept's 3.82 — 36% of the strand count at 146% of the prominence. That band is not trustworthy on this kid: on both sheets it spans the headband, whose two edges count as FALSE creases, so I re-ran it on a hair-only band. At 2-14% (bun crest and crown, above the band on both sheets) the concept reads 3.00 minima/row and the delivered reads 0.04 — 1% of the concept's strand count. At 2-22%, 1%. At 2-30%, 8%. The bun is a mathematically featureless dome, which the rubric caps at 4 on its own. Then the joins. (a) The bun butt-joins the crown on a hard shelf with a corner at both silhouette edges (front board 10x, x 220-330 y 55-115) and the toon outline pass draws it as a graphic line at gameplay scale in junebug-runtime-hero.png. (b) The hair tie is a FLAT QUAD SLAB, not a wrap: at 10x over magenta it is a single plane crossing in front of the tail whose lower edge is a hard flat cut with true background beneath it, and at gameplay scale in the run still it reads as a yellow tab stuck to the side of the head. (c) True background — alpha 0, sampled at (310,72) and (315,80) of junebug-profile-review.png — shows through the notch between the bun and the ponytail root, so the two masses do not touch; the tail hangs off the head through a narrow neck below the tie. (d) The tip blob. The 4 clauses it does pass are real and worth saying: the hairline is a proper sculpted widow's-peak that reads clean against skin from the front, there is no bare-skull read from any angle, and the headband arch itself is the best-authored accessory on the sheet.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The strongest sculpted category. Garments read as constructed at 5x on the A-pose board: the V-collar is a rounded piping TUBE rather than a painted line, the placket carries three raised button studs, the sleeves have two white stripes plus a real white cuff band, the belt is a band with two loops and a buckle, the knicker gathers into a darker cuff, the sock has its own band, and the shoe has a distinct lighter midsole slab and a red toe cap. The shoe's split is measured, not eyeballed: dominant tone 63.7% of the band against the concept's 64.7, second tone 31.1 against 27.2, mean saturation 34.9 against 36.8. Off 5 on the laces, which are three raised rectangular slabs on the vamp — they do not cross, have no eyelets and no weave, and on the right shoe of the front board one slab breaks the shoe's silhouette (x 160-390 y 590-710 at 4x). Secondary: the jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The face is a FORM, and I checked the specific things that separate a form from a sticker. A real nose breaks the profile with a defined tip and a nostril underside (junebug-profile-review.png x 210-320 y 110-240 at 8x). No decal-island seam anywhere — I looked for one at 8-10x on both the front and the profile and the atlas wraps the cheek and temple planes continuously. The ears are the best-constructed detail on the whole model: outer helix rim, inner concha shadow, and a lobe sitting against the skull, which settles 3.10 with no ambiguity. Features are legible at hero scale and the angled scowl brows still read at 40px. The chest patch I thought was a texture island at 4x is a specular gradient — resolved at 10x, not a defect. Held off 5 by the mouth. At rest it is a thin flat stroke a few pixels tall, close to the 'collapses to a line' the rubric warns about, and the expression RANGE does not survive: I pixel-diffed a 46x36 mouth box across the four runtime stills and grin/cheer/tongue are the same mouth (grin vs cheer 99 of 4968 channels differ by more than 12, max 39; cheer vs tongue 202, max 70) while only angry is distinct (650-669, max 120). Cropping the source atlas confirms it is the asset, not the capture instrument: cells 1, 10 and 11 are three near-identical open smiles, so the tongue cell has no tongue out and the cheer cell is no wider than the grin. All four stills are genuinely painted — byte sizes 291673/291988/292081/292276, a 0.2% spread, and all four show grass, sky and the character.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives both ends. At hero (junebug-runtime-hero.png, devstats reads 'model model', so this is the delivered GLB and not proxy evidence) the read is complete: scowl brows, big eyes, white headband arch, dark bun, tail swept to her left. I generated my own 40px read by resizing the front board to 40px tall, and every load-bearing element holds — dark bun over a white band, red top, pink pants, red socks, white shoes, and the angled brows are still two dark marks that say 'determined'. Off 5 on two counts. First, in the FRONT view at field scale the ponytail is entirely hidden behind her, so at 40px she is a bun-and-headband kid and the signature tail — the thing the turnaround draws an arrow at — contributes nothing to the read from the camera the fielder is most often seen from. Second, the tie reads at hero as a flat yellow tab rather than a wrap (junebug-runtime-run.png x 415-595 y 140-290 at 6x), which is a hero-scale accessory defect, not a hair-only one.

priorHumanReview.verdict: approved — reviewed the shipped model in production at https://srgirsky.github.io/recess-sports/ after rounds 5-7 rebuilt the shoe as one lasted upper, reshaped the ear, deepened the run's arm swing, mirrored the face columns and restored the splayed stance in every signature idle. The six category scores recorded here are the round-7 independent critic's, not the sculptor's.

The tongue cell shows no tongue out and the cheer is no wider than the grin, so three of the four emotional beats the draft card and the win/loss presentation lean on collapse to one read. Rubric 5.2; 3.14 itself passes (lips, teeth and tongue are all present and legible in the open cells).
junebug-runtime-swing.png captures swing_contact at the marker with EMPTY HANDS — no bat prop. It is fine as deformation evidence but it cannot show rubric 4.5's 'bat meets ball'.

The jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

NOT a defect, recorded so the next critic does not re-report it: the pale quad on the chest visible at 4x resolves at 10x as a specular gradient, not a texture-island seam. Ears are fully constructed (rim, concha shadow, lobe) and are the best detail on the model — EarSpec/build_ear are imported from sculptlib. The near-side eye in the profile board is foreshortened, which is correct for a true orthographic 90-degree view. All four runtime-face stills are painted.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is a MUSHROOM, not a ball cap. I measured both boards myself, alpha-thresholded row by row. Delivered front: cap max width 192px at row 175, then a 60px cliff to 132px at row 190, and the widest point of head-plus-hair below the cap is 144px (row 220) — head/cap = 0.75. Concept front view (spec box 86,391,129,871): cap max width 260px at row 246, head-plus-hair max width 271px at row 270 — head/cap = 1.04. That is a 29-point inversion of the drawing's own relationship: in the art the hair mass is the widest thing on the head and the cap sits down onto it; in the delivery the cap flares 33% wider than everything under it and background shows through the overhang on both sides in front, A-pose and the swing camera. Second defect, the bill: on the profile board the bill is a wafer of constant 8-10px section over a 58px projection (droop measured 24px over 56px = 23deg, so the 22deg droop and the 1.100 reach ARE fine as stated); on the concept sheet the profile bill is a contiguous run 41px thick at the tip (col 988) thickening to 66-68px at its root (col 946) over a ~44px projection. Normalised on head height (delivered 189px, concept ~254px) that is 4.2-5.3% section delivered against 16-27% concept — the bill is roughly twice as long and a quarter as thick as the drawing's, and in profile it reads as a knife blade or an antenna sticking out of the skull. The recorded note calls this 'a real forward duckbill'; it is not. Third: transitions are butt-joined primitives — shorts hem into thigh, sock into shoe, neck into collar are all cylinder-into-cylinder with a hard occlusion line, and the cap crown has a visible cone apex. Nothing is severed (no empty row inside the figure in any of the four boards) and the two legs are genuinely two legs.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The metered proportions pass and I re-took them: head height 34.6% vs concept 35.0 (delta -0.41, ok), head width:height 0.99 vs 1.05 (delta -0.06, ok), visible face left 26.6 vs 22.4 and right 27.1 vs 26.8 with asymmetry 0.52 (ok), ankle daylight 51.7 vs 56.9 (ok). So 6b.1/6b.3/6b.4 are green and rubric 3.13's aspect check passes. What holds this to 3 is the second half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms'. Cropped at 4x, the legs are smooth cones from the shorts hem to the sock top with no knee, no patella plane and no calf swell; the shorts hem is a flat cut with the thigh cylinder emerging from it; at rest in the A-pose and hero the shoulder is a soft lump and the sleeve is a straight tube to the cuff with no elbow form; the neck is a plain column meeting the collar at a hard ring. The concept's limbs are chunky toddler forms with an obvious calf and knee; the delivered limbs are markedly thinner relative to the torso even though the head ratio is in tolerance.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The worst category by a wide margin, and it is a construction failure, not a taste call. Band choice first: `npm run measure:strands -- calls_shot` at the DEFAULT 5-45% of head height reports concept 4.91 minima/row at prominence 16.9 against delivered 0.00 at 0.0 — 0% of count, 0% of prominence. But for THIS character the default band is crown-downward across the CAP (concept head 129-388, so the band is rows 142-245, i.e. cap dome to just under the brim), so its 0.00 is really 'the delivered cap dome has no panel seam and no texture', and on the concept side the 4.91 is partly cap seams and brim edge, not hair. I therefore re-ran on the rows where Theo's hair actually shows: 25-55% gives 0.84 vs 5.62 (15% of count, 159% of prominence) and 30-60% gives 1.14 vs 6.59 (17%, 176%). Those bands do reach the brows and the eye line, so some concept minima there are false creases (skin/hair and brow edges) — which makes 15-17% an OVER-estimate of what he carries, not an under-estimate. Cause verified in the builder, not inferred: `build_hair` in scripts/v2/blender/sculpt-theo-source.py uses `segments = 10` with `wave = 1.0 + 0.05 * cos(6 * theta)` — 1.67 columns per lobe against the ~4 Nyquist needs, and only 5% amplitude, so the wave is unrepresentable twice over. But the ratio is not even the real problem. `HAIR_LEVELS` maxes at `half_x = 0.455` while the skull's lateral half-width is `HEAD_RADII[0] * face_half_scale` = 0.400 x up to 1.08 = 0.432, so the entire hair shell is a skin-tight liner adding at most 0.023 (5%) of volume. The drawing's hair is the widest mass on the head (271px vs the cap's 260px); the delivery's is 144px against a 192px cap. Consequences, all cropped and looked at: the front board and the front A-pose board show TWO small dark triangular wedges at the temples plus two nubs below the ears and nothing else — no fringe, no hairline, bare skin across the whole forehead, temples and cheeks. In the four `-runtime-face-*.png` close-ups at 4x the hairline is a ragged sawtooth of dark specks along the cap edge that reads as dirt or stubble, produced by the piecewise `hair_window_z` step at |x|=0.42 sampled by only 10 columns. In `theo-runtime-swing.png` — a real gameplay camera, cropped at 5x — the back of the head is a small brown patch under the cap with a LARGE bare skin nape below it, and a skin-coloured ear form lying on top of the hair with a jagged seam. Rubric 3.3 bars a bare-skull read from any gameplay angle and requires the hairline to read from the front; both fail outright. The recorded note ('hair lifted to a legible deep brown with enlarged fringe wisps, ear-top flips both sides, and a covered nape in profile and swing views') is contradicted by the swing still it cites.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Three of nine measure:fidelity metrics are OFF and all three are the shoe: dominant tone of the band 88.4 vs concept 37.6 (tol 8), second tone 11.6 vs 61.4 (tol 8), mean saturation 13.6 vs 28.1 (tol 4). Cropped at 6x, the shoe is a near-white clog — a grey collar, three hairline lace straps, a tiny dark tick at the toe and a cupsole band barely a shade warmer than the upper; the concept's dark toe bumper and dark outsole edge are effectively gone. The sculpt script's own comment ('the charcoal saddle never reaches the bottom-9% window') and the recorded note ('shoe-band OFF cause accepted') explain the metric away, but the detector reads the CONCEPT's own pair as cream #ecddcc + tan #d9b68b at 37.6/61.4 — charcoal is not what it is comparing — and the saturation metric is independent of the split and also fails by 3.5x its tolerance. Second defect: the cap's cream team panel is a PAINTED GRADIENT, not a constructed edge. At front-board row 150 (cap 180px wide) the teal-to-cream ramp runs x196 (#9ea4a2) to x228 (#d7d2ca) = 32px = 18% of the cap width, per side; on the concept sheet at row 175 (cap 179px) the same boundary resolves between x197 (#39626d) and x202 (#fbedd0), i.e. under 5px = 2.8%. Six times too soft. Cause: `build_cap` colours 12 dome columns per vertex with `colour = TEAM_MASK if (frontness > 0.62 and z < 3.92) else TEAL`, so Gouraud smears the seam across a whole 30deg column. Judging TEAM_MASK on extent and placement only (not colour): placement is correct, centred front, but extent is over — the cream plateau is 45% of the cap width against the concept panel's 37%, and with the ramps the cream dominates ~80% of the cap face, where the drawing shows one crisp wedge of six. Third defect: in `swing_contact` five hard-edged cream parallelograms punch through the teal jacket back at mid-back; I sampled them at #bcb390 and #c1b99a against the jacket's #053d48, so they are cream-hued geometry (a tee or inboard sleeve ring emerging), not a teal specular — an interpenetration that reads at gameplay scale. Credit where it is due, which is why this is a 2 and not a 1: the jacket is genuinely constructed (separate shell with a fold-back front edge, a cream tee centre panel, cream sleeves, a striped rib hem, collar flaps), the socks have a proud roll with two crisp teal stripes, and the shoe does have a cupsole and lace straps.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The eyebrows are authored and invisible, and they are this character's signature. I opened `assets/v2/source/theo-face-atlas.png`: every one of the 16 cells carries a pair of thick black brows, and not one of them renders in any still — front board, front A-pose board, hero, run, and all four `-runtime-face-*.png`. The reason is geometric and the script states the numbers itself: the brow anchor lands at z 3.304, while the cap dome's lowest ring is z 3.290 with half-widths 0.650/0.595 and y_centre -0.030, so the cap shell sits in front of the brow row from any front-facing camera and swallows it. Cropped at 6x, `angry` and `grin` differ by mouth alone — the eyes and the (absent) brows are identical — and Theo's cocky arched brow, present in all five concept views, never appears. On the positive side: all four expression stills ARE genuinely painted, not stubs (294,526 / 295,659 / 297,025 / 296,299 bytes, within 1% of each other, no 29% empty-canvas file), and rubric 3.14 passes on its own terms — the grin opens with teeth, tongue shows a tongue, cheer opens, angry frowns, all legible at draft-card crop. The nose is a real form (`nose_push`, verified in the builder) and it does break the profile — but on the profile board it reads as a sharp triangular beak rather than the drawing's small upturned button, and the socket dish is so shallow that the eyes read as flat decals with a soft blur. A face-island seam is visible as a dashed scribe down the cheek just in front of the ear in the grin still. Ears are constructed, not bumps — `EarSpec(center=(0.020, 3.230), radii=(0.1550, 0.1650))` and `build_ear` are both present, and the profile crop shows a rim, an inner hollow and a lobe — but the form is a crescent flange with a hard dark notch behind it and, in profile, its front edge sits almost against the eye decal with no cheek between them.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Hero (`theo-runtime-hero.png`) does report `model model` at 28.5k tris, so 4.1 is satisfied and this is model evidence — but the read it delivers is 'a kid in an oversized two-tone bowl', with no hair and no brows anywhere on the head. Every distinguishing mass the drawing gives him except the cap is missing, and the cap's own shape is the mushroom described above, so at hero he is interchangeable with any other cap kid. The 40px strip on the board is a pale blob over a pale body with a darker band across the middle: the highest-contrast element in the concept — the black hair mop that in the drawing is 271px wide against a 260px cap — contributes zero pixels at 40px, so there is no memorable read left to survive (3.9 fails). Separately, the integration evidence is both stale and a proxy: `docs/v2/concepts/theo-in-game-review.png` was last written by commit 97a17cd (2026-08-09) while the boards come from 4875d2c (2026-08-15), and the image shows capsule arms with sphere caps, ball-jointed black legs, slab feet and a floating cream V on the chest — the proxy body, not the shipped GLB. Section 4.1's rule is that proxy evidence is never fidelity evidence, so section 6 is effectively unwalked at this revision.

polishFindings: Hair is a skin-tight liner, not a mass: HAIR_LEVELS max half_x 0.455 against a skull half-width of 0.432 adds 5% of volume, so the front and A-pose boards show only two temple wedges and two sub-ear nubs over bare skin. The drawing's hair is WIDER than the cap (271px vs 260px); the delivery is 144px against a 192px cap. Fix the radii before touching the wave.

The cos(6*theta) wave at segments=10 is 1.67 columns per lobe at 5% amplitude — unrepresentable twice over. Trade hair ROWS for COLUMNS at constant triangle cost (the grizz precedent) and sharpen the crease profile; do not just raise the amplitude.

hair_window_z's piecewise step at |x|=0.42 sampled by 10 columns produces a ragged sawtooth hairline that reads as dirt or stubble in all four -runtime-face-* close-ups at 4x. Needs either more columns or a smoothed window.

Bare skull from a real gameplay camera: theo-runtime-swing.png cropped at 5x shows a small brown hair patch under the cap with a large bare skin nape below it, plus a skin-coloured ear form lying over the hair with a jagged seam. Rubric 3.3 forbids this from any gameplay angle.

Cap reads as a mushroom, not a ball cap: front-board cap 192px over a 144px head-and-hair (0.75) where the concept is 260px over 271px (1.04). BRIM_HALF_W 0.390 is only 57% of the cap's 0.688 half-width, so the dome overhangs the bill by 43% per side and background shows through the overhang on both sides.

The bill is a wafer: 8-10px section over a 58px projection on the profile board (4.2-5.3% of head height) against the concept's 41px tip and 66-68px root over ~44px (16-27%). Twice too long, four times too thin. REACH 1.100 and 22deg droop are fine as recorded — thickness and section are the defect.

The cap's cream team panel is a painted gradient: 32px of ramp = 18% of cap width per side at front-board row 150, against <=5px = 2.8% on the sheet. Cause is per-vertex colour on 12 dome columns via `frontness > 0.62`. Extent is also over (45% plateau vs the concept panel's 37%). Judge on extent and placement only — placement is correct.

Every one of the 16 face-atlas cells carries thick black brows and none render: the brow anchor at z 3.304 sits inside the cap dome, whose lowest ring is z 3.290. angry and grin currently differ by mouth alone, and Theo's signature arched brow never appears.

Cream geometry punches through the teal jacket back in swing_contact — five hard-edged parallelograms at mid-back, sampled #bcb390/#c1b99a against #053d48. A tee or inboard sleeve ring emerging; check the Spine/Spine2 weighting of the inboard ARM_STATIONS and the tee loft against the jacket shell.

Shoe fails all three of its metrics (88.4/11.6 split vs 37.6/61.4, saturation 13.6 vs 28.1) and at 6x reads as a white clog: the dark toe bumper and outsole edge are effectively absent and the cupsole is barely a shade off the upper. The script comment about the charcoal saddle missing the bottom-9% window explains the wrong thing — the detector compares the concept's own cream/tan pair, and the saturation metric is independent.

No knee, no calf, no deltoid, no elbow: limbs are smooth tapered cones and the shorts hem, sock top and collar are butt joints with a hard occlusion line. This is what holds proportions to 3 despite every AUTO proportion metric being green.

In profile the ear's front edge sits almost against the eye decal with no cheek between them, and the crescent flange has a hard dark notch behind it. EarSpec and build_ear ARE present with a rim, hollow and lobe, so 3.10 is met in construction — the placement and shape are the issue, and I did not measure the concept's ear position, so treat this as an eye note.
The profile nose reads as a sharp triangular beak rather than the drawing's small upturned button. nose_push exists and does break the profile; the tip exponent is too pointed.

Section 6 integration evidence is stale AND a proxy: theo-in-game-review.png was last written by 97a17cd (2026-08-09) while the boards come from 4875d2c (2026-08-15), and it shows capsule arms, ball-jointed black legs, slab feet and a floating cream V. Re-capture it against the shipped GLB.

Not defects, checked and cleared so nobody re-files them: nothing is severed (no empty row inside the figure in any of the four boards); the legs are two legs with daylight between thighs and calves and the AUTO ankle metric is in tolerance; all four -runtime-face-* stills are genuinely painted (294.5-297.0KB, within 1% of each other); the near-side eye's foreshortened look on the profile board is what a true 90deg orthographic view predicts; and the grey-brown nub at the nape on the profile board is a lit hair flip tube (#584d49 / #4c2e17), not a hole or a foreign object.

The recorded 4/5s are unsupported by the evidence they cite: 'no bare-skull read from any angle' is contradicted by the front board, the A-pose board and the swing still; 'a real forward duckbill' is contradicted by the measured 8-10px section; 'a covered nape in profile and swing views' is contradicted by the swing crop; and 'shoe-band OFF cause accepted' argues against a charcoal comparison the detector never made.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The profile is good (zoom-profile-review.png: a big cambered wheel with rim, hub and 8 spoke arms, a real seated tuck) but the FRONT is where he lives on a draft card, and there the chair evaporates. Measured on zoom-front-review.png at 72% of figure height (row 503, the wheel line): each wheel occupies 18px of a 168px-wide silhouette (10.7%), against the concept front view's 80px of 300px (26.7%), and the row is six disconnected slivers where the concept is one solid mass. Camber IS authored (sculpt-zoom-source.py:413, WHEEL_CAMBER=0.115 over a 0.55 radius = ~6.5 deg) but at that value the wheel renders as a black vertical slab, so no sport-chair splay reads. Silhouetted with no colour the front view is a head, a torso and four vertical sticks - nobody identifies a wheelchair.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The two metrics that carry on a seated figure pass and I reproduced them: head 29.9% of figure height vs concept 31.6 (-1.76, ok) and head w:h 1.08 vs 1.06 (ok). What fails is the rubric's second clause, 'joints read as connected forms'. There is no knee: build_seated_legs (sculpt-zoom-source.py:378-401) joins a horizontal thigh tube to a vertical shin tube with only a SHORTS_DARK hem lip, so the front view (zoom-front-review.png, x 232-253 and 286-307, y 455-635) is one unbroken bare cylinder from shorts hem to shoe with no knee, calf or ankle. And the hip is a butt-joint: cropping the same 220x200px hip region from zoom-runtime-hero.png and zoom-runtime-run.png at 5x gives PIXEL-IDENTICAL images, confirming the whole lower body is ROOT-weighted furniture that an animated torso cone is simply set down on top of.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Not a blob and not bald - I checked the bare-skull claim by sampling columns x=230/245/262/280/300 down zoom-front-review.png and the hair-to-skin transition is a clean 2-3 row edge at y~188, and the swing still (zoom-runtime-swing.png, head crop at 6x) shows the nape shell holding from behind. So it clears the hard bars. It fails the 'one designed mass' bar: measure:strands reports 3.95 strand minima/row vs the concept's 5.92 (67% of the count) at mean prominence 64.7 vs 17.9 (362%) - too few, far too fat. Delivered is a symmetric fan of ~8 flat paddle fins butt-joined to a thin cap that covers only the top ~20% of the head with both temples bare; the concept is a dense one-directional back-sweep with a fringe wedge over the brow. That lost fringe is exactly what the measured face-left metric reports (concept 0.00 vs delivered 32.9). Spike tips are flat-capped tubes, visible at 6x from behind.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The shoes settle it. Each foot is three tubes (sculpt-zoom-source.py:395-401): a SHOE lozenge and a WHITE lozenge under it. In the front crop (zoom-front-review.png x 232-307, y 555-600 at 4x) they read as two blue spheres sitting on a grey plank; in profile they are a blue slab on a white slab. No toe box, no heel curve, no sole edge, and none of the concept's two teal velcro straps. Nothing else is constructed either: the teal raglan panel is an airbrushed vertex gradient across the chest rather than a panel with an edge, the shorts are a navy block, there is no collar rib and no shorts cuff. Only the sleeve cuff ring (TRIM at SLEEVE_HEM_X-0.020) actually reads. The chair's frame is spindly wire tubing (0.030-0.036 radius) against the concept's chunky moulded tube, and the casters are bare black tori with no hub.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: 3.14 passes - all four zoom-runtime-face-*.png stills are legible at draft-card distance with real teeth (grin) and a real tongue (tongue). But this is a sticker on a ball. Measured nose projection off the profile silhouette's left edge: minimum x=218 at y=252 against a 221-222 brow/cheek plane, i.e. 4px on a 198px head = 2% of head height; the concept profile projects 13px on a 130px head = 10%. Five times too shallow, and in the front board render and in ALL FOUR hero-close face stills there is literally zero nose - flat skin between eyes and mouth. nose_push sits at nz -0.20 -> z 2.843, only 0.02 above the mouth anchor 2.823, so it is authored at the lip line rather than between eyes and mouth. Island seams facet visibly across the cheeks at 5x, the eye decal wraps past the profile silhouette edge as a white sliver, and a stray atlas fragment (dark arc + highlight, ~8x14px) prints on the neck cap above the collar (zoom-profile-review.png 250,275 at 14x). Ears are NOT absent - build_ear/EarSpec confirmed at sculpt-zoom-source.py:34,137,487 - but EAR_SPEC center=(0.020, 3.000) puts them above the eye anchor (2.983) at mid-head depth, so they read as pale fins on the cheek instead of ears behind the jaw.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: 3.9 fails outright. On the 40px strip in zoom-fidelity-review.png the chair is completely gone - at full res the wheels are 18px of a 168px silhouette, so at 40px they are sub-pixel; what survives is a blue blob with a head and two pale stripes, which is any kid on the roster. His one memorable read is the chair and the chair does not survive to field scale. At hero it is better but still wrong in kind: no clip in the library puts a hand on a push rim. Idle, run and swing (zoom-runtime-hero/run/swing.png) all show a standing kid's arm action swinging in space while the chair sits motionless underneath - the hip crops are pixel-identical across idle and run. He reads as a kid parked in furniture, not an athlete driving it, which is the whole point of the only wheelchair user on the roster.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The clump term modulates RADIUS: x = half_x * clump(theta) * cos(theta), y = y_centre + half_y * clump(theta) * sin(theta). In an orthographic front or profile view the halo's outline at a given z is the extremum over theta of that expression, which lands near theta=0 / pi where cos(6t)=cos(10t)=1 for every row and every amplitude. So the outline is always half_x*(1+a6+a10) - one number per z-level, ten z-levels, ten straight facets. No amount of theta-modulation can scallop that outline; it can only shade the interior. The code comment's promised payoff ('grouped clumps with a scalloped silhouette instead of a smooth dome') is unreachable by construction. What Mimi needs is z-modulation (a per-row radius wobble, or real proud tufts) or an outline built from separate clump volumes, not a finer theta term. The halo is still roughly twice as column-locked as the drawing, and the raw top-K number that the last critic quoted (80.6%) is not comparable across the two images because K differs (3 vs 13) and so does its chance baseline. Chance-corrected, delivered 35.0% vs concept 17.4% over the default 5-45% band; effective columns 19.59 of 48 vs the concept's 44.60; 24 of the 48 bins carry ZERO creases in any row, while two bins (7 and 40 - the left and right shading rolloffs) carry 33% of all of them. On the tighter crown-only band (5-30%) it is worse: 15.14 effective columns of 48. Row-to-row persistence is 80.9% vs 82.7%, which looks like parity until you correct for chance (2.89 creases/row vs 12.67 gives baselines of ~17% and ~55%), after which it is 77% vs 61%. So yes: the minima DO wander with row now, exactly as the comment claims - they just have almost nothing to wander in, because the modulation never becomes a visible crease in the first place. The headline 23% is inflated by the band. measure:strands' default 5-45% of head height reaches down past the fringe onto the forehead and brows, and those hard skin/hair and brow edges are counted as strand creases. Re-run on hair only: 5-30% gives 19% of the concept's count, 5-20% gives 18%. The honest number for the crown is ~19%, at 116-156% prominence.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: NEW DEFECT, and it is a floating accessory (3.8). build_hoodie_details puts the hood at ellipsoid centre (0, 0.360, 2.480) with radii (0.300, 0.180, 0.250), so its top reaches z 2.73 - above the shoulders, where the body is only NECK_LEVELS' 0.116-0.158 half-depth. Result: in both profile views the hood is a red ball behind the neck with genuine BACKGROUND between it and the body. Cropped at 8x over a green matte and confirmed: an unbroken green wedge separates hood from torso from the hood's crown down to ~40% of its height, ~8 px (0.06 ft) at its widest, alpha-verified (transparent runs of 8-10 px at y 274-290 in mimi-mash-profile-apose-review.png). At the runtime toon camera the same separation prints as two dark navy slashes flanking the neck in every face still. The cream tee sliver (surface_patch at z 2.545-2.600) reads as a flat white bar taped across the collarbone in every board and runtime still, not a collar. The kangaroo pocket reads in profile as a rectangular slab butt-joined to the front of the torso with a hard undercut and a visible shadow gap, at 5x. Neither is a hole; both are the 'butt-joined primitives' 3.1's 5/5 and 3.4's whole criterion rule out. Judged as extent, not colour, per the trap. The TEAM_MASK ring is one 0.030-ft-tall roll station (z 0.520) on top of two CUFF stations and a PANTS_DARK lip - the accent is a thin top ring, the roll body is its own grey-blue, which is the correct Grizz sock-roll construction and the correct answer to the round-2 full-cuff blocker. On the board the whole roll is ~16 px of a ~200 px lower leg, proportionally matching the turnaround's double roll. No finding. The one problem with the roll is that it crosses BOTH legs as a single band, which is a symptom of the fused-legs defect, not of the mask.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: PARTLY CONFIRMED, and misattributed. There is no decal-island seam inside the skin on the board: a strict skin-only horizontal-gradient sweep of rows 150-255 finds no step that is not adjacent to hair, and a 16x crop of both temples shows continuous shading across the cheek. What IS there on the board is a stair-stepped HAIR EDGE: at 16x the right temple's hair/cheek boundary descends in 2-4 px jogs with a rectangular notch partway down - the curl shell's fringe silhouette, aliased by its 10 rows and 48 columns. BUT the seam the last critic described is real at the runtime face camera: mimi-mash-runtime-face-{cheer,tongue,angry}.png all show an unmistakable stepped polygon boundary around the face island, lighter inside than out, with visible corners at both temples and above the brows. I could define it, so I did, and I ran the same detector over concept and delivered. Take measure-strands.mjs's own per-row crease detector (contrast-stretch the row to 0-255, smooth by 3, keep local minima of prominence >= 6) and, instead of only counting them, record each crease's position u as a fraction of that row's hair-mass width. Quantise u into 48 bins - one bin per mesh ring column. Then report three things: (a) TOP-K SHARE, the fraction of all creases falling in the K busiest bins where K = round(mean creases per row), reported against its own uniform-chance baseline K/48 and chance-corrected as (C - K/48)/(1 - K/48); (b) EFFECTIVE COLUMNS, exp(entropy of the bin histogram), i.e. how many distinct columns the creases actually occupy; (c) ROW-TO-ROW PERSISTENCE, the fraction of creases that recur in the next row within +-1.5 bins. A perfect flute scores 100% / ~K / 100%. A drawing of real curls scores near chance / ~48 / near chance.

polishFindings: Stop modulating theta. The outline is the only place a toon character's hair reads, and the outline is built from CURL_LEVELS. Either (a) push the row table itself in and out so consecutive z-levels alternate proud and tucked - that scallops the front and profile outline directly, costs no triangles, and is mirror-safe because it never touches theta; or (b) spend triangles on a handful of real proud tuft volumes at the rim, which was tried and rejected as 'floating rectangular tabs' - but that verdict was about tabs, not about tufts that intersect the shell. Column count is spent; 6826 of 7000 leaves nothing anyway.

polishFindings.finding: The clump term modulates radius as a function of theta only, so it can never touch the front or profile outline - the outline is the per-z extremum, which sits at theta=0/pi where both cosines are +1 for every row. Ten z-levels give ten straight facets and a flat-topped dome. 48 columns bought interior shading that the smooth normals and the soft key then erase.
polishFindings.evidence: 6x contrast stretch of the crown band shows only the two terminator rolloffs; 24 of 48 crease bins are empty; effective columns 19.59/48 vs concept 44.60/48; silhouette RMS 11.74 pp with the crown +11 to +18 pp too wide.

Joints do not read as connected forms anywhere: no neck (head sits on the tee collar in grizz-profile-apose-review.png), no elbow, no knee, no ankle (the sock is a collar on a peg, grizz-front-legs region y 556-600), and the shoe is 8.6% of figure height vs the concept's 6.9%.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: measure:strands reports 1.61 strand minima/row against the concept's 15.55 — 10% of the drawing's strand count. It is worse than the rubric's 'smooth featureless blob' cap: the mass is FACETED, with flat polygon planes readable at hero scale (grizz-runtime-swing.png, upper-left of the crown, x 470-560 y 150-230) and a pinched cone apex. The hairline is a hard horizontal shelf across the forehead (grizz-front-review.png y=200-210) where the concept draws an irregular fringe near the brows. And the measured colour is wrong: delivered hair median #4a4540 (a neutral mid grey, chroma 0.085) against the concept's #1c140f (near-black, chroma 0.25), while the tee matches almost exactly in the same pair of renders (#8c502c vs #8e5228) — so the lift is authored, not exposure. On a character whose entire identity is the afro, a grey faceted blob with no curl relief is not a 4.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The shoes carry this category and carry it honestly — a constructed sole band, toe cap and slouch-roll sock read in grizz-profile-review.png (y 560-646), and measure:fidelity puts the shoe tone split inside tolerance (dominant 82.4 vs 81.9, second 17.6 vs 16.0, saturation 18.7 vs 19.4). Nothing else is constructed: the chest pocket is a flat stamped rectangle with a hard border and no flap or stitch (grizz-front-review.png x 218-250 y 330-360); the shorts have no waistband and no hem at either leg opening — and the single alpha run means there is one hem line across one tube, not two leg openings (crop of x 170-370 y 470-670); the laces are three painted tan rectangles on the vamp rather than laces through eyelets (grizz-profile-review.png y 595-615); the sleeve is a cylinder butt-joined to the arm with a rim step.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The face is a decal island and it reads as one. In all four grizz-runtime-face-*.png stills a faceted plane change runs across the forehead and down the cheeks, bounding a quad that holds every feature; there is NO NOSE at all in the front or 3/4 read (grizz-front-review.png y 245-275, and every face still between the eyes and the mouth is blank plane) — the profile's small bump is the only nose in the asset. The feature cluster sits high with a large blank jaw beneath it. Worse, brows and eyes are PIXEL-IDENTICAL across grin, cheer, tongue and angry — only the mouth changes, so at draft-card size all four expressions read the same. And the expression is inverted against the sheet: the concept (grizz-turnaround.png front head, x 60-360 y 120-420) draws heavy-lidded half-closed eyes and soft down-and-OUT brows (sulky, napping); the model has wide-open round ovals and hard black down-and-IN chevrons (angry). (2) THE BUN IS BUTT-JOINED, MEASURED: on the front A-pose the silhouette width jumps 78px -> 121px between rows 147 and 151 - a 43px ledge in four rows where the bun meets the crown. The concept sweeps curls continuously into the knot. (3) The bun is a visibly faceted 7-gon in both front and profile at 3-4x crop, and the shirt hem and shorts read as butt-joined prisms. (4) On the runtime run still the collar-to-shoulder wedge reaches the outline and bites a black notch out of the shoulder contour (cropped at 6x, region x490-640 y290-430 of bendy-bao-runtime-run.png). Head aspect is fine: 164/210 = 78.1% wide vs the concept's 198/242 = 81.8%, delta only -3.7 points, so 3.13 is not the problem.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The one category I can defend at 4. measure:fidelity honestly REFUSED the head-height and head-aspect family for this kid ('no neck pinch' - his pinch sits inside the T-pose arm band), so I took the geometry myself off the A-pose front, where the arms are down. Crown (bun top) row 87; the silhouette narrows 114 -> 82 -> 72 -> 60px across rows 267-279, which is a clean jaw-into-neck pinch at row 279, giving head-plus-bun = 192/561 = 34.2% of figure height; against the authored 87-297 span it is 210/561 = 37.4%, and the concept's own declared band is 242/646 = 37.5%. Either way this is a chunky child head at roughly a third of the figure, matching the turnaround and not the proxy. Head width:height 78.1% vs concept 81.8%. Limbs are short, the shoes are chunky, the neck seats under the jaw, and the bind pose reads as connected forms. Two things keep it off 5: the T-pose and A-pose arms run slenderer than the concept's chunky forearms, and the shoulder joint stops reading as connected in motion - the run still opens a dark wedge with a bright backface sliver exactly at the collar-to-shoulder junction, so the joint that is fine in bind is not fine in the delivered clip.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: This is the category the ruler settles against the recorded 4. I ran measure:strands myself at three bands and state them all. DEFAULT 5-45%: delivered 1.54 minima/row at prominence 24.9 vs concept 6.48 at 17.4 = 24% of the concept's strand count. That default band reaches down onto the forehead and brows, where the skin/hair boundary and the painted brow edges are counted as FALSE creases, so it flatters the delivered figure. Re-run on the BUN AND CROWN ONLY: 2-28% band gives 0.86 vs 6.09 = 14% of the concept's count at 74% of its prominence; 5-30% band gives 0.88 vs 6.79 = 13% at 80%. Excluding the brows the delivered mass carries roughly one seventh of the drawn strand grouping, and unlike the roster pattern its prominence does not over-compensate (74-80%, i.e. the few creases that exist are also shallower than the drawing's). That is a smooth featureless mass, which the rubric caps at 4 by itself. It goes to 3 because the silhouette is ALSO wrong: profile head depth 70.5% vs the concept's 80.2%, a 43px-in-4-rows hard ledge where the bun butt-joins the crown, and a bun that crops as a faceted heptagon rather than a knot. Worse, in the delivered run and swing stills the mass reads as a round afro mop with a bump on top, not the tidy swept knot the sheet draws - the gameplay read of his signature hair is a different hairstyle. THE OLD BACKFACE-VOID BUG IS GENUINELY FIXED, verified by my own samples: front bun (85,73,64) against adjacent crown hair (85,71,60); profile bun (50,42,37); runtime bun (31,21,7) against side hair (23,13,0). Warm brown-black everywhere, no slate-grey void, from the ascending-level-table regression. Hair does not swallow the face: centre-column hairline sits at 38.6% of head height delivered vs 36.8% measured on the concept front figure (head centre x=217), a 1.8-point match, and brows, eyes and mouth are all clear of it.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The construction vocabulary is genuinely present - teal ringer neckband, teal sleeve cuffs, raised hem with trim, sock roll-top band, laced two-tone sneakers with sole rims - and I re-ran the shoe metrics myself: dominant tone 64.2 vs concept 67.6, second tone 35.8 vs 31.6, mean saturation 28.3 vs 28.7, all three inside tolerance. Stripe carriage on the board is fine too, which surprised me: torso greenness amplitude 26.9 over ~4 bands delivered vs 25.7 over ~4 bands on the concept, so the washed-out look is a runtime-tonemapping story, not a missing stripe (runtime hero torso still measures 45.9 amplitude with two clear peaks). It scores 3 anyway, because the garment VISIBLY FAILS on the delivered animation evidence. THE WORST DEFECT ON THIS CHARACTER: bendy-bao-runtime-swing.png carries a jagged ink-navy TEAR across the lower back of the tee, immediately above the waistband - cropped at 7x over x470-630 y460-520 and again at 7x over x480-610 y480-580, it is a lightning-bolt-edged rip roughly 40% of the shirt's width, the navy shorts' waistband ring erupting through the shirt surface in swing_contact. At gameplay distance it reads as a hole torn in his shirt. Second: the collar-to-shoulder wedges, which I sampled on the board front at (240,300) = 110,103,93 and (298,300) = 78,73,65 against the shirt beside them at (265,310) = 198,205,195 - a 2-2.5x luminance drop flanking the neck - become, in the run still, a black notch on the silhouette edge with a bright cream backface shard inside it (6x crop, x490-640 y290-430). Third, smaller: the sleeves are plain cream with a teal cuff where the sheet continues the stripes across the shoulder, and the cargo pocket flattens to a faint facet in true profile.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: 3.14 passes convincingly and I checked the byte-size trap first: the four runtime-face stills are 291578 (grin), 290790 (cheer), 290063 (tongue) and 289578 (angry) bytes - all within 0.7% of each other and none near the ~29%-of-sibling size an unpainted canvas shows - and cropping each at 6x confirms four genuinely distinct, draft-card-legible mouths: grin opens on a white tooth band, tongue adds a red tongue below the teeth, cheer opens on a dark red interior, angry closes to a frown under down-angled brows. Features are legible at hero scale and the face is visible in the front board view, so the 4 bar is met and I score it 4. It can never be 5, and both blockers are measured. (1) THE NOSE. From the front it is simply not there: an 8x crop of x220-330 y200-290 on bendy-bao-front-review.png shows unbroken cheek between the lens rims and the smile, no tip, no nostrils, no form shadow, and the same is true in all four runtime face stills. In profile I traced the front silhouette myself: the frontmost SKIN pixel is x=209 at rows 238-241 (the glasses rim owns x=213 at rows 199-235, so I stepped past it), against forehead skin at x=220 on row 196 - 11px of projection over a 210px head = 5.2%. The identical trace on the concept profile figure gives a nose peak of x=947 at rows 294-298 against a forehead of x=930 = 17px over a 242px head = 7.0%. The delivered nose is 74% of the drawn projection and reads as zero from the camera the game actually uses. (2) A visible decal-island seam runs temple-to-chin down the near cheek where the flattened face plane meets the round skull - clearest in the 6x run-still crop and present in every face still. Brows are flat black paint and the eyes are flat decals. ON THE RECORD'S LENS REQUIREMENT, checked and deliberately NOT filed as a defect: I grepped build_glasses in scripts/v2/blender/sculpt-bendy-bao-source.py and there is no lens-disc geometry at all - the builder emits two cyclic tubes, two temple arms and a bridge, with the comment 'Open rings - the atlas eyes read through them'. But the SKILL.md rule exists for sheets that FILL the rings with paper-cream shine, and a 5x crop of the concept face shows Bendy Bao's lenses are clear: skin, sclera, iris and highlight all read through at full opacity. Open rings are the drawing-correct construction for this kid, and the visible-face metric that would arbitrate was refused by the instrument, so no one should quote a number here either. THE TEMPLE-ARM REQUIREMENT IS MET: the arm bows outboard to side*0.470 in the builder, and it is visibly present in the render - a 10x crop of x240-310 y195-265 on the profile shows the dark wire crossing the cheek and terminating at the ear root, not buried inside the skull.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: At hero the identity triad reads - top knot, round ink-dark frames, striped tee - and the review page reports 'model model', so this is fidelity evidence and not a proxy. At 40px it does not hold up as a 4. The board's own zoom strip loses both glasses and stripes; what survives is a dark bump, a pale torso, dark shorts and tan shoes, which is a generic kid silhouette. Bendy Bao IS the glasses kid, and the one feature that names him is the first thing to go at field scale. Worse, the fallback identity carrier fails too: in the run and swing stills the hair mass reads as a round afro mop with a bump, not a swept top knot, so at gameplay distance he is competing with every other dark-haired kid on the roster rather than being read as the bespectacled one. The runtime tee measures a healthy 45.9 greenness amplitude at the torso centre, but the bands wash toward white on the lit side and contribute nothing below hero scale. Add the two runtime artifacts that are visible at exactly this distance - the torn shirt back in swing_contact and the black notch bitten out of the shoulder in run - and the field read is actively damaged rather than merely thin.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The front board is recognisable; the PROFILE is not, and 3.1 scores both. Concept profile (turnaround panel 3, cropped 4x): an open face - forehead, a projecting button nose, philtrum, lips, chin, a clean jawline to the neck, and a large fully-exposed ear - with the mane swept behind it. Delivered profile: a featureless auburn egg. I measured the visible skin against the head silhouette in both with one detector: concept 91.5% of head width at its widest row (skin bbox 200x217 over a 200px head, 100%), delivered 46.4% (bbox 80x193 over a 153px head, 52.3%). Half the profile read is gone - no chin, no jaw, no mouth, no cheek, only a thin crescent along the leading edge with one eye and a nose tip. Profile head depth is 27.8% of figure height against the concept's 32.1%, so the skull is also ~13% shallow front-to-back (3.13). Transitions are not organic either: the mane is one ring loft that butt-joins the collar with no neck visible in profile at all, where the concept shows a clear neck between jaw and ringer collar. NOT severed and NOT holed - I flood-filled all four board renders: zero fully-empty rows inside the figure bbox in any view, zero enclosed background regions in profile, front-apose and profile-apose, and 2 regions totalling 6px (antialias) in front.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Child proportion is broadly right in the A-pose front board and 1.4/featurelatitude are AUTO-green, so I make no bobblehead claim. The failure is 'joints read as connected forms'. Cropped at 8x, the hero arm is a plain tapering cone from shoulder to hand: no deltoid, no elbow, no wrist. It exits the sleeve as a hard step - the cream cuff ends and a visibly thinner skin tube begins, with a dark outline gap between arm and torso - and at 9x on the front board the hand is a flat paddle with three finger grooves and no thumb. The concept's toddler-chubby girth is absent; the recorded note concedes 'limbs read a notch slimmer' and then scores 4 anyway. Compounding it, the mane mass dominates the figure at gameplay angles: in the swing_contact still the head-plus-hair egg spans roughly 52% of the visible figure height from behind and swallows the shoulders and the whole bodice.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured, and it fails in BOTH directions. Strand grouping: I ran measure:strands myself at the default 5-45% band and at four tighter bands to rule out fringe/brow contamination - 5-45%: 2.92 vs 5.86 minima/row = 50% of concept count at 251% prominence; 15-45%: 3.40 vs 5.84 = 58% at 233%; 10-40%: 47%; 20-60%: 46%; 5-30%: 37%. The deficit is band-independent, so it is not a detector artifact. The cause is confirmed in source: ring_loft_mane uses segments = 18 with clump = 1 + curl*sin(8*theta) - 2.25 columns per lobe, barely above Nyquist, so most of the clump is literally unrepresentable and the creases that survive are over-deep (2-2.5x prominence) instead of numerous. Volume: I measured the mane's max width on the A-pose board at 152px over a 550px figure = 27.6% of figure height (matching MANE_LEVELS max half_x 0.545 over a 3.92 figure = 27.8%, so the number is right), against the concept front panel's mane at the full 242px figure width over a 630px figure = 38.4%. The mane carries 72% of the concept's width. The rubric caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 'however correct its silhouette' - this silhouette is NOT correct: too narrow, faceted, with a blunt hard-cut bottom edge where the concept has scalloped S-wave tips. And it over-covers where it should not, erasing the profile face (see 3.1). Below the cap.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I verified it at 8x rather than assuming: a crisp cream waistband with hard top and bottom edges (a constructed edge, not a painted gradient - I checked the transition specifically and it is a clean two-row step) carrying a genuinely sculpted five-point gold star, a cream ringer collar and cuffs, striped socks, a two-tone sole with a visible welt, and lace strokes. On colour I defer to the number: measure:fidelity puts the shoe band's dominant tone at 50.2 vs the concept's 51.9, the second tone at 49.8 vs 45.0 and mean saturation at 26.6 vs 25.9, all inside tolerance, so I make no shoe-split claim. What holds it at 3 is that the signature garment is unbuilt: the skirt is a smooth featureless cone with a flat straight hem where the concept's defining garment is a pleated A-line with visible vertical pleat folds and a scalloped hem. The laces are single 1-2px dark strokes with no eyelets, no tongue and no crossings (cropped at 14x - they read as stray dark specks), and the cream is a soft instep dome rather than the concept's stitched rubber toe cap.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Three defects, one of them an evidence failure. (1) dazzle-runtime-face-grin.png IS EMPTY - 82,133 bytes against 276,780 / 277,339 / 277,497 for angry / cheer / tongue, i.e. 29.6%, exactly the empty-frame signature. Opened, it is the DOM HUD on pure black: no field, no sky, no character - the WebGL canvas never drew. Cheer, angry and tongue are genuinely painted and their mouths do read at that distance (open mouth with teeth, a frown line, a tongue), but 3.14's four-still evidence is 3 of 4 and one expression is unverified. (2) The face is a DECAL ISLAND WITH A VISIBLE SEAM. Cropped at 6x from the runtime hero, the face plate is a distinctly lighter orange patch bounded by a hard polygonal edge running from the brow down the near cheek to the jaw, plus a straight vertical seam on the far cheek, and the brow is a floating dark bar whose end is cut flat on that boundary. Rubric 3.5 names 'no visible decal-island seam' as the test and this seam reads plainly at hero scale. (3) Expression is unreadable in profile: 46.4% visible skin at the widest head row vs the concept's 91.5%, with no mouth, no lips and no chin surfacing at all, so at every profile-ish gameplay angle the face has nothing to express with. To be fair to the asset and against its own recorded note: a nose DOES exist and DOES break the leading edge of the profile silhouette - that note is wrong in the asset's disfavour.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px zoom strip does carry the one memorable read - brown mane over purple dress - and identity survives it. The hero close-up survives too, but only as a face peeking out of a wig, and it is where the seam (3.5) and the ear spike (3.10) are most visible, so the close-up actively costs the character. On the field: at 16x on the runtime hero the hands are the same warm orange as the infield dirt and effectively disappear into it, which is a 6.6 risk on a fielder. Held at 3 rather than lower because the silhouette is unmistakable at both ends of the range.

measuredFidelity.result: RUN MYSELF. measure:fidelity -- diva (concept front 242x630, delivered 452x549; shoe tones read off concept #f6ece1 and #f2cda3): shoe band dominant tone concept 51.9 / delivered 50.2 / delta -1.66 ok; second tone 45.0 / 49.8 / +4.74 ok; band mean saturation 25.9 / 26.6 / +0.73 ok; daylight between ankles 0.00 / 34.0 / +34.0 OFF (tol 12) - per 6b.4 read as stance, the concept panel has the ankles touching and the delivered bind pose stands wide, the legs are unambiguously two legs so 3.12 PASSES; five metrics NOT MEASURED (head height % of figure, head width:height, visible face left, visible face right, face L/R asymmetry) because the head/neck detector found no silhouette pinch between crown and shoulders - a fact about the drawing, not a pass.  measure:strands -- diva, BAND USED: I ran the default 5-45% AND four others precisely because the default can reach past the fringe onto forehead and brows where skin/hair and brow edges count as false creases. 5-45% (default, concept head rows 191-398, delivered 99-319): concept 5.86 minima/row at prominence 36.3 over 84 rows, delivered 2.92 at 91.0 over 89 rows => 50% of count, 251% of prominence. 15-45%: 5.84@42.0 vs 3.40@97.7 => 58% / 233%. 10-40%: 5.94@36.8 vs 2.79@82.3 => 47% / 224%. 20-60%: 7.44@47.9 vs 3.44@92.2 => 46% / 193%. 5-30%: 5.43@26.6 vs 2.04@53.8 => 37% / 202%. Band-independent; I report 15-45% as the cleanest (below the fringe, above the brow band at 37%).  MY OWN MEASUREMENTS (same detector both sides): mane max width, delivered A-pose board 152px over a 550px figure = 27.6% of figure height (cross-checked against MANE_LEVELS max half_x 0.545 over a 3.92 figure = 27.8%), concept front panel 242px over a 630px figure = 38.4% => the mane carries 72% of the concept's width. Profile visible skin at widest row: concept 183px over a 200px head silhouette = 91.5%, delivered 71px over a 153px head = 46.4%; skin bbox concept 200x217 (100.0% of head width), delivered 80x193 (52.3%). Profile head silhouette depth: concept 32.1% of figure height, delivered 27.8% (13% shallow). Severance/holes flood-fill on all four board renders: front y98..647 - 0 empty rows, 2 enclosed background regions totalling 6px (antialias); profile, front-apose, profile-apose - 0 empty rows, 0 enclosed regions. NOTHING IS SEVERED, 3.7 PASSES. Face-still byte sizes: grin 82,133 / angry 276,780 / cheer 277,339 / tongue 277,497 - grin is 29.6% of its siblings and is confirmed empty on inspection. Source values read, not assumed: ring_loft_mane segments = 18 with sin(8*theta) clump = 2.25 columns/lobe; EAR_SPEC center z 3.220 radii (0.125,0.150) with head span 3.99->2.68 => ear centre at 58.8% of head height; HEADBAND_ARC ends at z 3.440 = 42.0% of head height, tube radius 0.046.
measuredFidelity.note: Feature placement gated by featurelatitude: brow 37.25 vs traced 37.0, eye 54.1 vs 54.1, mouth 76.3 vs 76.1 through her declared 3.99-2.68 span (the spec refuses all three landmarks - the mane merges every band - so the targets are bounded traces). No earLine: the mane owns the width metrics; ears reviewed by eye.

polishFindings: THE 'NO earLine' CLAIM IS FALSE, and it is the load-bearing one. scripts/v2/turnaround-specs/dazzle.spec.json records landmarks.earLine = { value: 78.3, unit: pctOfHead, proudPctOfHead: 17.4, confidence: 'traced' } - the tracer found it and calls it traced, while brow, eye and mouth are the three it refused. The sheet plainly draws ears: cropped at 4x, the concept profile panel shows a large ear with an outer helix rim, an antihelix, a concha shadow and a lobe, sitting PROUD of the hair with the mane tucked behind it, and the same ear is visible in the three-quarter panel. Yet scripts/v2/featurelatitude.lint.test.js (diva entry, ~line 240) omits earLine on the stated ground that 'the widest row is the mane at 78.3%, hair on concept and delivery alike; her ears hide under the curtains' - the sculpt header repeats it at line 85. By that file's own comment at line 156, an entry without earLine SKIPS the ear check, so nothing gated the placement.

CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED: EAR_SPEC center z = 3.220 puts the ear centre at 58.8% of the 3.99->2.68 head - eye level, as the sculpt comment says - against the sheet's traced earLine of 78.3% (mouth level). The ear sits ~19.5 points of head height too HIGH, ungated.

3.10 FAIL (and 3.8 FAIL). The ear is NOT absent - I grepped and it is built: sculptlib.ear is imported at line 33, EAR_SPEC declared at line 137, build_ear called per side at line 620. It is BURIED and CLIPPING. In the profile board only two disconnected skin-coloured slivers surface through the mane (a small crescent and a tiny arrowhead, z 3.14-3.36, matching EAR_SPEC's z extent 3.07-3.37); in the runtime hero and run stills, cropped at 6x, it protrudes from the hair silhouette at the temple as a sharp pointed elf-ear spike. No rim, no inner shadow, no lobe against the skull from any angle - the exact 3.10 anti-pattern, arrived at from the opposite direction (not a bare ellipsoid bump but a shard of one).

NOT A DEFECT - I checked before reporting it. The pale cream annulus with a skin-toned, folded centre on the lower-rear head in dazzle-profile-review.png (original px x250-285, y284-317, i.e. z 2.36-2.60) initially reads as a button or a gouge. Cropped at 9x it is the near HAND plus its cream sleeve cuff, seen end-on down the T-pose arm pointing at the camera, exactly as a true 90-degree orthographic profile should show it. It is absent from the A-pose profile board, which confirms it. No artifact.

TEAM_MASK judged on EXTENT only, never colour (the headband is the declared team-accent surface - grey #D8D2C6 on the board, gold at runtime). Its extent is short: HEADBAND_ARC terminates at z 3.440 = 42.0% of head height, so the band stops on the crown above the eyes and never comes down beside the face. The concept draws a WIDE FLAT RIBBON that runs from the crown down past the temple to the top of the ear at ~78% of head height, roughly 2.5x the width of the delivered 0.046-radius round tube. Front-on this makes the delivered band read as a thick pale saddle across the crown rather than a hair ribbon.

Garment colour boundaries are CONSTRUCTED EDGES, not painted gradients - verified at 8x on the waistband, which steps cream-to-purple across two rows top and bottom with the sculpted gold star seated on it. The soft transitions elsewhere (sock stripe, skirt) are lighting, not colour ramps. This item passes and the round-1 'mushy gradient' repair held.

The skirt is a smooth cone with a flat hem - no pleats, no scalloped hem - against a concept whose signature garment is a pleated A-line. Same defect the recorded note concedes ('the colour-pleat wedges read only softly') while scoring 4.
Shoe laces are single 1-2px dark strokes with no eyelets, tongue or crossings; cropped at 14x they read as stray dark specks on the upper and vanish entirely at 40px.
Skin tone is very close to the infield dirt in the runtime stills; at 16x the hands are nearly indistinguishable from the ground. Worth a 6.6 check at gameplay camera.

swing_contact renders bat-less on the review page. I did not score it - the bat is likely a game-side attachment, not the GLB - but if the board is meant to be 4.5/4.2 evidence, a contact still with no bat cannot show a marker landing on 'bat meets ball'.
EVIDENCE MUST BE REGENERATED before any re-score: dazzle-runtime-face-grin.png is an empty frame and 3.14 cannot be assessed on four expressions until it is recaptured.

The recorded card asserts 'no nose breaking the hair-covered profile'. That is wrong in the asset's own disfavour - nose_push does build a real button nose and it does break the profile silhouette's leading edge. The profile's problem is the mane covering the jaw, not a missing nose; fixing the wrong thing would regress a feature that is already right.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The gross read is right (egg dome, big round glasses, noodle neck, boxy striped tee, straight jeans, rolled cuffs) and the proportion metrics are green, but the two forms the sculpt script itself says 'carry the whole silhouette' both fail. (1) THE EARS DO NOT REACH THE OUTLINE. I measured the delivered front render (540x720, figure bbox y88-647): the head silhouette is widest at 162px at y187 - the DOME - and the ears break the outline only at rows 221-222, by 10px per side. At the traced ear line (57.9% of the 88->260 head band = y188) the right ear's outer edge is x342 while the skull edge is x349, so the ear is 7px INSIDE the outline and contributes nothing. The concept is the opposite: its head is widest AT THE EARS (229px at y252-262 vs 189px at y235 just above them), the ears exceed the skull for 60 rows (28.7% of head height) by 20px per side, and the repo's own trace records earLine proudPctOfHead 10.3 - delivered is 5.8% at the wrong latitude and 0% at the right one. Ears are BUILT (EarSpec/build_ear at line 541, radii 0.160/0.190) and in profile they do carry a rim and an inner concha shadow - this is a misbuilt, too-shallow, too-low ear, not a missing one. (2) THE PROFILE IS A FLAT WALL. In noodle-profile-review.png the entire face front from y153 to y200 sits on one dead-straight column at x=207 - that is the glasses ring seen edge-on with zero wrap - and the nose advances it to x=203 only at rows 200-211: 4px, 2.4% of the 165-row head band. The concept profile advances from x943 (lens line) to x959 (nose tip), 16px = 7.7% of its head band, three times as much. Credits: head depth/width 139/162 = 0.858 against the concept's 198/229 = 0.865, near-exact; NO severed rows in any of the four board renders (I ran a full row scan on front, profile, front-apose and profile-apose: zero rows with no figure pixels inside the bbox); legs are two legs. Held to 3 on the ear and the flat profile, plus the butt-joined shoulder wedge and the ankle 'napkin ring' called out below.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The numbers are in tolerance and I re-took them: head height 29.0% vs concept 31.0% (delta -1.99, ok), head width:height 0.99 vs 1.04 (delta -0.05, ok). The child proportion and the signature over-long thin neck read correctly and the neck sits organically into the skull with no collar seam. What holds this at 3 is the second half of the rubric line - 'joints read as connected forms'. Both shoulders fail it, and they fail it where a player looks: in noodle-runtime-hero.png the far shoulder carries a hard-edged navy wedge roughly 20x25px at native scale, outlined by the rim shader so it reads as a TEAR in the tee, and the near sleeve cap is a butt-joined tube pushed into the torso with a crease instead of a deltoid. The same wedge is present and larger in noodle-runtime-run.png, where the far shoulder reads as a detached dark lump with its own outline floating off the torso. The hand at run is a stack of hard-edged bars separated by black outlines rather than a fist. Torso mass is also thin against the head: A-pose shoulder span 146px against a 162px head, and the T-pose torso below the armpit runs only 72-86px, so the head is 1.9x the torso's width.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Abstained - null. NOODLE IS BALD; there is no hair mass to score and no hair surface is built (the script declares HAIR = #3A2A1C explicitly as an 'unused surface lane - he is bald; brows are atlas ink'). The bald negative space itself is intact in the board renders: one uninterrupted dome, no invented cap, no hairline seam, no hole. I did NOT run measure:strands, per the brief. One consequence of baldness belongs to other categories rather than here and is recorded there: because the crown is his own skin, the dome's faceting and its warmth shortfall land on the largest single surface he has.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I verified the edges are constructed rather than painted: scanning down x=268 through the tee, every stripe boundary transitions in 1-2px (329->331, 348->350, 371->373, 392->394, 416->418) - these are vertex-colour edges, not gradients. Rolled jean cuffs exist on both legs, band y572-592 = 3.6% of figure height against the concept roll's 4.4%, correctly placed at the ankle on both legs (TEAM_MASK, judged on extent and placement only - the untinted grey on the board and the tinted olive at runtime are both expected). Wrist cuff band, cream cupsole and two cream lace straps are all built (straps=((-0.170,-0.122),(-0.060,-0.012)) in NOODLE_SHOE). Held at 3 for four things. (1) THE SHOE IS NOT A LACED LOW-TOP. Cropped at 6x front and 7x profile, the two authored straps render as flat cream stripes on the outer quarter; there is no throat, no eyelets, no tongue, no collar opening and no separately readable toe bumper. The concept shoe has four lace crossings, metal eyelets, a cream toe cap and a dark chevron; the delivery is a tan clog with racing stripes. The rubric names laces explicitly. (2) The dark navy wedge at both sleeve/torso junctions reads as a hole in the garment at hero and run scale (see headBodyProportions). (3) The jean cuff is a smooth ring WIDER than both the jean leg above it and the shoe below it, with a hard step at each end and no fold edge - a napkin ring, not a rolled hem. (4) Garment warmth is largely gone: the cream stripe delivers rgb(210,207,202), r-b = 8, against the concept's rgb(229,208,183), r-b = 46 - 17% of the concept's warmth - and the blue stripe delivers b-r = 19 against the concept's 36. Denim itself is fine, rgb(74,103,137) vs concept rgb(52,78,105).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Below the floor, and the cause is a mis-traced landmark that the gate then certified against itself. THE MOUTH IS ~9.5 POINTS OF HEAD HEIGHT TOO HIGH. The repo's own machine trace, scripts/v2/turnaround-specs/noodle.spec.json, records landmarks.mouth = { value: 78.9, row: 288, confidence: 'traced' }. My own luminance map of the concept confirms it exactly: the smile is the dark run at row 288, and rows 261-264 - which the sculpt script and featurelatitude.lint.test.js both cite as 'the small smile rows 262-270' - are his NOSTRILS (the nose bulb runs ~245-264). featurelatitude.lint.test.js's own header warns about precisely this failure mode ('...NOSTRIL not the lip line, so it reports the mouth 10 [points] high'); Noodle's hand-entered mouth: 69.4 is that mistake hard-coded, so the record's 'mouth 69.4/69.4 green' is the sculpt agreeing with its own error, not with the drawing. On the delivered render the mouth line is row 207 of the 88->260 head band = 69.2% - faithful to the wrong target. THE CONSEQUENCES ARE THE WHOLE CATEGORY. The smile sits directly under the lens rims with no philtrum, and the nose has nowhere left to live: in noodle-front-review.png, cropped at 8x across x230-310/y185-245, the region between the lenses is UNMODULATED SKIN - no bulb, no nostrils, no cast shadow, only a scatter of freckle dots - against the concept's large highlighted button nose with two dark nostril slits. nose_push IS built (line 128, 'centre nz -0.42'), so this is a nose too shallow and too low, not an absent one: in profile it is a 4px hard-edged wedge at rows 200-211, i.e. AT the mouth's own latitude, and it projects 2.4% of head height past the frame line where the concept's projects 7.7%. Eye-to-mouth spacing collapses to 11.4% of head height (iris centroid row 187.5, mouth row 207) against the concept's 25.3% (iris 233.5, mouth 288) - 45% of the drawing's - leaving the features crammed in a band under the glasses and the bottom quarter of the face blank. The measured visible-face shortfall follows: 35.6/35.6 against 45.4/44.0, OFF by 9.8 and 8.4 on a tolerance of 6, and at that sample row the delivered head is crossed by irises (11px and 9px), sclera and four frame crossings while the concept's same row is 88.6% clean skin. Expression: all four -runtime-face-*.png stills are genuinely painted and distinct (295-296 KB each, no undersized sibling - grin shows a teeth band, cheer an open O, tongue a pink tongue, angry a closed line), but in ALL FOUR the eyebrows are hidden behind the lens rims at the gameplay camera, so angry and neutral differ only by a flat mouth stroke and angry does not read as angry. At hero the near lens reads as a dark socket and the temple bar is the boldest mark on the face.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives at hero - bald dome plus big round glasses plus blue/cream stripes is unmistakable from front, three-quarter and behind - and that is what keeps this off a 2. Two things hold it well below approval. (1) THE DOME IS VISIBLY FACETED. Cropped at 4x from noodle-runtime-hero.png, the skull shows large flat polygon facets with hard shading breaks across the crown and occiput, and the same faceting is present in every runtime still (run, swing_contact, and all four face cells). On the one character whose crown is his own skin and his largest single surface, this is the first thing the eye lands on. (2) THE SKIN LOSES ITS WARMTH BAND, which his record says is load-bearing for him. I sampled the delivered board's upper dome at (250,110) 40x20: rgb(225,203,179), r-g = 22, sat 0.20, and 0% of that patch passes the project's own isSkin test (it fails sat > 0.22). The concept's dome at (195,150) 40x20 is rgb(253,208,154), r-g = 45, sat 0.39, 100% isSkin. Cheek: delivered r-g 29 / sat 0.31 against concept r-g 70 / sat 0.58. Across rows 96-148 of the delivered front render only 30-41% of the head row classifies as skin, against 99-100% on the concept. At runtime the same skin renders ochre/mustard and drifts toward the infield dirt. At 40px (board strip, cropped at 4x) the bald pale head and the striped shirt carry, but the glasses survive only as a faint grey smudge - his one memorable cue is at the edge of legibility, leaving a single-cue read.
