polishFindings: MOUTH LATITUDE IS TRACED WRONG AT SOURCE, and the gate certifies the error. scripts/v2/turnaround-specs/noodle.spec.json records landmarks.mouth = 78.9% (row 288, 'traced'), but sculpt-noodle-source.py's header and featurelatitude.lint.test.js both assert 69.4% ('the small smile rows 262-270'). Rows 261-264 of noodle-turnaround.png are his NOSTRILS, not his lips - the exact confusion featurelatitude's own header documents. Fix the hand-entered 69.4 to the traced 78.9, drop the smile ~9.5% of head height, and the nose finally has room; leaving it green is how a 2 passed as a 4.

NOSE READS AS NOTHING FROM THE FRONT. nose_push (line 128) is built but so shallow that an 8x crop of x230-310 / y185-245 on noodle-front-review.png shows unmodulated skin between the lenses - no bulb, no nostrils, no cast shadow. In profile it is a 4px hard wedge at rows 200-211 that projects 2.4% of head height past the frame line against the concept's 7.7%, and it sits at the mouth's own latitude. Deepen it and lift it once the mouth moves down.

EARS DO NOT REACH THE FRONT SILHOUETTE. EarSpec(center=(0.020, 3.280), radii=(0.1600, 0.1900)) is built and the profile ear has a rim and a concha shadow, but in front the ear's outer edge (x342) sits 7px inside the skull edge (x349) at the traced ear line, and breaks the outline only at rows 221-222 by 10px. The traced spec wants proudPctOfHead 10.3 and the concept's head is widest AT THE EARS. Push the ear outboard and up to the 57.9% line so the dome stops being the widest row.

BALD DOME IS VISIBLY FACETED at hero. A 4x crop of the head in noodle-runtime-hero.png shows large flat polygon facets and hard shading breaks across the crown and occiput, repeated in run, swing_contact and all four face cells. On the one crown that is its own skin this is the first thing seen; the head needs more rings/columns or smoothed normals.

SKIN STILL FAILS THE WARMTH BAND ON THE DOMINANT SURFACE, whatever the recorded 'do not fix the palette again' note says. Delivered dome rgb(225,203,179), r-g 22, sat 0.20 - 0% of that patch passes the project's own isSkin (sat > 0.22) - against the concept's rgb(253,208,154), r-g 45, sat 0.39, 100% isSkin. Rows 96-148 of the front render classify only 30-41% skin per row against the concept's 99-100%. If the authored swatch genuinely cannot go warmer without clipping r, the fix belongs in the board/runtime ramp, not in another chroma round - but it is not fixed, and it is why the 40px read loses the head's skin identity.

SHOULDER SEAM WEDGE, both sides, and worse than 'a polish item'. A 6x crop of noodle-runtime-hero.png at (480,300) shows a hard navy triangle roughly 20x25px at the far sleeve/torso junction, outlined by the rim shader so it reads as a tear in the tee; a 5x crop of noodle-runtime-run.png at (500,300) shows the same shape larger and detached-looking. Cross-character (Bendy Bao, Flash) - fix in sculptlib's arm cap / shoulder blend.

SHOE HAS NO LACING READ. Both authored straps ((-0.170,-0.122), (-0.060,-0.012)) render as flat cream stripes on the outer quarter; 6x front and 7x profile crops show no throat, no eyelets, no tongue, no collar and no separately readable toe bumper, so a laced low-top reads as a slip-on clog against the concept's four lace crossings and metal eyelets.

DARK SPIKE ACROSS THE MIDSOLE ON BOTH SHOES. Cropped at 14x from noodle-front-review.png at (216,620) 34x30: a black-brown diagonal sliver about 2px wide and 6px long runs from the tan upper down across the cream cupsole and ends in a point, and the mirror of it sits on the other shoe near x316. Symmetric, so it is geometry (toe-cap or strap end) punching the midsole, not a render artifact.

GEOMETRY SPUR AT THE SHOE TOE IN PROFILE. Cropped at 16x from noodle-profile-review.png at (295,615) 30x26: a 2-3px tan/brown tab projects out of the shoe's toe edge at mid height, past the silhouette, into the background. Small but it is a poke-through.

ANKLE CUFF READS AS A NAPKIN RING. The TEAM_MASK roll is a smooth cylinder wider than both the jean leg above it and the shoe below it, with a hard step at each end and no fold edge or denim doubling. Extent and placement are right; the construction is not.

EYEBROWS ARE HIDDEN BEHIND THE LENS RIMS AT THE GAMEPLAY CAMERA in all four -runtime-face-*.png stills, so angry and neutral differ only by a flat mouth stroke and angry does not read as angry. All four stills are genuinely painted (295-296 KB each, none undersized). Either raise the brows on the atlas or shrink/lower the lens rings.

GARMENT WARMTH IS ALSO WASHED OUT: the cream stripe delivers r-b 8 against the concept's 46 (17% of it) and the blue stripe b-r 19 against 36. The tee reads near-neutral grey on the board where the drawing reads warm cream and blue-grey; same ramp story as the skin, and worth checking together.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Front reads as a kid with a spiky crown and is recognisable without colour, so the large read survives. Three things hold it at 3. (1) The profile silhouette has NO nose break at all: in turbo-profile-review.png the leading edge from fringe to chin is one continuous convex curve. nose_push IS built (sculpt-turbo-source.py:117, 'the tiny button nose', tip 0.075) so this is a misbuilt/under-scaled nose, not an absent one — but the concept's profile figure has a clear nose bump breaking its outline and the delivered has none. (2) The hair is a smooth skullcap with eleven isolated cones pushed through it — the butt-joined-primitive read the rubric's 5 explicitly excludes, and here it is visible at hero, not just under a loupe; the concept is a layered swept mop of overlapping tapered locks with a scalloped outer edge. (3) The lower silhouette is one leg, not two: in both bind and A-pose the thighs, calves and ankles fuse into a single tapering column and the two shoes butt into one continuous slab separated only by a faint seam (4x crop of x180-360,y420-710 of turbo-front-review.png). Measured: ankle daylight concept 0.75 -> delivered 0.00. Idle and run do splay the legs, so the recorded rig-splay cause covers part of this, but thighs and calves interpenetrating is beyond splay. No severance: I scanned all four board views for a row or column of pure background crossing the figure and found zero empty rows and zero empty columns inside the silhouette (span y89-646 in each).

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: measure:fidelity could NOT take head height %, head width:height, or the three face-visibility metrics — the detector found no silhouette pinch between crown and shoulders. That is itself the finding: this kid has no neck. The head sits straight onto the collar ring, and in profile the jaw and the shirt overlap with only an under-chin shadow between them. Overall child proportion is otherwise close to the turnaround — big head, short body, high hip — and that part is fine. What fails the category's second clause ('joints read as connected forms') is the limbs: the A-pose front and profile show arms as uniform tapered cylinders with no deltoid mass at the shoulder and no elbow swell, the blue sleeve reads as a separate ring cylinder slipped over the arm rather than fabric continuous with the shirt, and the hands are tiny paddle nubs with only faint finger lines. In the swing_contact still the lead arm is a straight stick with a sharp kink where the elbow should be a form. This is the 3.11 EYES item failing, not just an aesthetic quibble.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: MEASURED and band-robust. measure:strands at the default 5-45% band: delivered carries 54% of the concept's strand count at 364% of its prominence. Re-run at 5-30%: 44% / 275%. Re-run at 10-35%: 53% / 380%. I checked trap 5 before filing: at the delivered head span 89-282 the 5-45% band is rows 98-176, entirely inside the spike zone and upper cap and well above the fringe at ~row 200; at the concept head span 101-362 it is rows 114-218, also all hair. The band is clean on both sides, so the numbers are about hair, not brows or forehead. What the numbers describe is exactly what the crops show: the concept's mop is many overlapping tapered locks each carrying fine internal grooves, while the delivered is a featureless smooth cap with eleven deep isolated cone gaps — half as many groupings, each gap three to four times deeper. The rubric caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 however correct its silhouette; here the cap is featureless AND the silhouette has swapped the concept's swept mop for a radial sea-urchin, several cones pointing rearward and downward. Add a hard stepped polygonal hairline over the forehead — a staircase of straight edges with square notches, plainly visible at 3.2x in turbo-front-review.png and at 7x in the runtime face stills — where the concept has a soft pointed fringe. One designed mass, yes; no bare-skull read from any angle, yes; but it is not the concept's hair and it has no strand grouping. 3.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuine construction credit: the sleeve ends in a real geometric cuff band (7x crop of x150-270,y280-370 shows a darker ring with its own lip, not a painted gradient); the collar is a constructed rib ring visible in front and profile; the shoe is properly built with a sole slab, a side panel and a lace flash; the sock has its own band. I checked the garment colour boundaries specifically: they are constructed edges with real geometry lips, NOT painted gradients — the shirt/shorts boundary at 7x (x195-345,y420-500) is a flat rim with a distinct darker lip. Against that: the shirt body is a smooth flared smock with no waist, no side seam and no chest or back indication, and its hem is a flat chopped disc butt-joined to the shorts with zero drape and zero overhang, so the tee never reads as hanging over the waistband the way the concept's does. The shorts are the bigger miss — a plain untextured truncated cone with no hem band, no cuff, no pocket line and no stitching, where the concept's are unmistakably constructed denim with visible top-stitching, a pocket and a hemmed leg opening. Half the outfit is built and half is primitive volumes. 3. TEAM_MASK (judged on extent and placement only, never colour): small symmetric wedges at the shoulder tops plus the collar ring — a sensible small yoke, correctly placed, not sprawling.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The single worst area, and the defect is specific. The concept's strongest facial feature after the hair is a pair of bold, thick, arched eyebrows sitting on bare forehead, clearly separated from the fringe in BOTH the front and profile concept figures. Trap 1 checked: the brows are not absent — every one of the 16 cells in assets/v2/source/turbo-face-atlas.png carries a heavy black brow, and sculpt-turbo-source.py:78 traces them to atlas rows 245-260. They are BURIED. The fringe is set so low over the face island that at 7x on turbo-runtime-face-grin.png and -angry.png only the bottom one-to-two-pixel sliver of each brow escapes the hairline, and it reads as part of the hair, not as a brow. The consequence is that the angry cell — whose entire signal is the angled brow, since its mouth is a small flat frown — does not read as angry at hero scale, let alone at draft-card distance. The script justifies this deliberately at line 138 ('The spec REFUSES brow and eye — the fringe merges them'), but the drawing is the target and the drawing does not merge them. Second defect, and this one is measured: the ear. Trap 1 checked — build_ear/EarSpec IS used (line 33, 133, 576), so it is misbuilt, not missing, and at 10x it does show an outer rim edge and a shallow inner dish, so 3.10 technically passes, weakly, with no lobe read and an almost invisible concha shadow. The problem is scale and placement. Delivered ear width in profile is ~67px against a head depth of 118px at that latitude = 57% of head depth. The concept's profile ear is ~36px against a head depth of 179px = 20%. That is 2.5-3x oversized. EAR_SPEC radii (0.170, 0.200) against HEAD_RADII (0.400, 0.420, 0.420) confirms it independently: 40% of head depth and 48% of head height in world units. And EAR_SPEC center y=+0.020 against HEAD_CENTER y=-0.020 puts the ear forward of the head's centre, so it lands on the cheek rather than behind the jaw — in the runtime hero 3/4 crop it is a flat tan fin covering the entire cheek and it is the first thing the eye lands on. Third: no nose break in profile (see silhouette note). Passing items: no decal-island seam anywhere, the nose is real modelled geometry rather than a sticker, the socket dish integrates the eyes with the skull, and 3.14 passes cleanly — the grin has a lip line with a tooth band, the tongue cell opens a real mouth with a tongue, and all four -runtime-face-*.png stills are genuinely painted (275,333 / 275,589 / 276,978 / 275,810 bytes — no ~29% outlier). Trap 4 checked and NOT filed: the near eye in the true 90-degree profile appears as a narrow foreshortened almond, which is what foreshortening predicts; the only other dark mark on the profile temple is the outer tip of the buried brow, consistent with the brow finding.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px strip on the fidelity board passes — the dark spiky crown over a blue shirt survives the shrink and is the memorable read, and the character does not vanish against grass or dirt in the runtime stills. Identity survives at hero too. What holds it at 3 is that both ends of the range are degraded by the same two defects. At hero the giant flat ear paddle dominates the 3/4 read and the brows are gone, so the face that a draft card has to sell is eyes-nose-mouth on a bare oval. At field scale the hair silhouette that carries the identity is the eleven-cone urchin rather than the concept's swept mop, so the 40px read is memorable but is memorable as a different kid. The run and swing stills are the strongest evidence on the sheet — legs separate cleanly, feet plant, the pose has real energy — which is what keeps this at 3 rather than lower.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Front reads: round glasses, open brown jacket over cream, blue jeans, dark hair. Profile does not. The hair in profile is an angular faceted SLAB -- a flat vertical back plane, a flat front plane, hard chamfered polygon corners at the crown -- reading as a cardboard box, not the turnaround's rounded, layered, swept mass. Verified at 8x on the-professor-profile-review.png and -profile-apose-review.png; the facets are 18-column ring-loft edges, not compression. Rubric 3.1's five asks for organic transitions and this ships the opposite: the sleeve terminates at the wrist in a bare diameter STEP (front-review.png x20-230 y265-335 at 4x) with no cuff form, a literal butt-joined primitive. The jacket in profile is a smooth cone that flares continuously from chest to a hard horizontal hem cut, with no waist -- the turnaround's cropped bomber silhouette is gone. NOT severed anywhere: neck, wrists and ankles are continuous in every crop I took. Legs are NOT fused -- 3.12 passes with clear daylight between thighs and calves in bind, A-pose and run (measured daylight 14.5 vs concept 0.00, and per 6b.4 that is the concept's legs-together DRAWING, not a sculpt fault). Ears pass 3.10 outright: the profile crop shows a genuine outer rim, an inner shadow and a lobe against the skull, not an ellipsoid bump.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The strongest category and the only one I would sign. Measured myself: head height 31.1% of figure vs the concept's 32.3% (-1.19, ok); head width:height 1.04 vs 1.00 (+0.04, ok) so 3.13 passes and no bobblehead. Child proportion, not the proxy. Legs read as two legs. Shoulders hold a rounded deltoid through swing_contact and run rather than collapsing to a hinged cylinder, and the elbow line stays continuous in the run still. One deduction from 5: the wrist and the shoulder are diameter steps rather than connected forms -- the sleeve is a constant-radius cylinder shoulder-to-wrist with no taper and no elbow mass, so the joints read as joined tubes rather than connected forms, which is exactly what 3.2 asks about.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I grepped the builder rather than inferring it, and the premise handed to me is understated. ring_loft_sweep is called exactly ONCE (sculpt-the-professor-source.py:619) and is the only hair geometry in the file -- no clump pass, no lobe pass, nothing. Inside it the ring is x = half_x*cos(theta), y = y_centre + half_y*sin(theta): a plain ELLIPSE per row, 18 columns, with ZERO lobe or crease modulation authored at all. There is no 6-lobe clump to be under-sampled; there is no clump. So the only minima measure:strands can find are the 18-facet polygon corners, and it reports 2.54 minima/row against the concept's 8.87 -- 29% of the count at 168% of prominence. I re-ran at 5-28% (30%) and 5-22% (27%) to strip the forehead and brow contamination the default 5-45% band can reach; the ratio does not move, so the shortfall is the hair, not the instrument. Rubric 3.3's own words -- 'a smooth featureless blob caps at 4 however correct its silhouette' -- put the ceiling at 4, and three further faults take it below: (1) the concept's asymmetric side-sweep is gone, SWEEP_BIAS 0.085 is imperceptible and the delivered mass reads as a symmetric mushroom bowl; (2) the hairline over the forehead is a jagged blocky STAIRCASE with a castellated rectangular step at centre, plainly visible at 8x and at hero scale (it is skin showing through, not background -- not a hole); (3) it swallows the face, see below.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely split. The shoes are the best-built thing on him and I will not mark them down: cream sole with a raised toe bumper, a taupe canvas upper, three cream lace stripes and an eyelet tab, over properly rolled cream jean cuffs -- constructed footwear, matching the turnaround's read. I also confirmed a collar exists in profile with a stitch line and a small collar point, and the open jacket's fold-back front edges do read. Per the record's warning I did NOT treat the shoe colour as a finding: all three shoe metrics came back ok (dominant tone -3.33, second tone +6.46, mean saturation -2.69), the drawn grey upper sits above the bottom-9% band the metric samples, and the delivered upper reads taupe rather than the concept's cooler grey only by eye. The jacket is where it fails. Against the turnaround: no zipper (the concept draws a full front zip with a pull), no pockets (the concept draws two prominent flap pockets with buttons on both front views), no ribbed cuff (a bare diameter step instead), no ribbed waist hem band, and no back yoke seam (visible in the concept's back view, absent in the swing_contact rear still). Roughly half the constructed detail on the SIGNATURE garment is missing, and without the waistband the jacket reads as a flaring labcoat rather than a cropped bomber.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The worst category, and it is measured. BOTH EYEBROWS ARE COMPLETELY BURIED UNDER THE FRINGE in every single delivered frame -- front board, A-pose, hero, run, and all four expression stills. They are authored (face-specs.mjs the_prof browY 21, browThick 4.6, browHalf 13) and the sculpt script itself calls his brows 'the boldest mark on a face', so this is an occlusion fault, not an omission. I measured it: scanning hair-tone coverage per row across the head, the CONCEPT opens forehead skin past 25% of head width at 30% of head height and is 43% hair / 54% skin by the traced brow latitude of 44.4%; the DELIVERED is still 87% hair at 40%, 62% hair at the 44.2% brow latitude, and does not open past 25% skin until 42.9%. The fringe descends about 13 percentage points of head height lower than the drawing's, over a brow line the sheet keeps clear. The consequences are not cosmetic: (a) at 12x a hair wedge with a hard straight chord cuts across the viewer-right lens and eats the outer half of that eye and part of the iris -- geometric interpenetration, not a shadow, which is a 3.8 failure at hero scale; (b) rubric 3.14 fails on one of four cells -- grin, cheer and tongue are properly built (upper teeth, an open dark interior with a lower-lip highlight, a pink tongue breaking the lip line, all four stills distinct by md5 and all ~280KB, none empty) but ANGRY is indistinguishable from neutral apart from a small downturned mouth oval, because the brow is the only carrier of anger on a toon face and his never renders; (c) the profile shows no eye, no brow and no mouth at all. This also explains both OFF metrics I ran: visible face left of centre 25.3% vs 11.9 (+13.4) and right 25.3% vs 14.2 (+11.1) -- the delivered brow row is bare skin where the concept's is brow ink. Credit where due: the nose DOES break the profile silhouette (verified at 8x, a distinct wedge -- 'no nose' would have been a false finding), the eyes and round frames read strongly head-on, and asymmetry measures 0.00.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: At hero the review page confirms 'model model' (4.1 satisfied) and the round glasses plus the brown-over-cream torso carry him -- but the fringe throws the eye region into shadow at the gameplay 3/4 camera, so the eyes read as two dark smudges and the face has no brow to anchor it. At the 40px strip his one memorable mark, the round wire glasses, is sub-pixel and gone; what survives is dark blob hair, a brown/cream torso split and blue legs, which is a generic read rather than a specific one. 3.9 is therefore weak: he survives the hero close-up on the glasses and loses at 40px, and the rubric asks for both. Fielder visibility against grass and dirt is fine -- the dark hair and mid-brown jacket separate cleanly from both in the runtime stills.

Adding lobes into the same 18 columns will not help (the instrument's own header records this); columns, or a sharpened crease profile, is the lever.

In profile the hair is a faceted angular SLAB -- flat back plane, flat front plane, hard chamfered crown corners. It reads as a box. This is the single largest gap between the delivered profile silhouette and the turnaround's.

The jacket is missing most of its construction: no zipper, no flap pockets (the concept draws two with buttons), no ribbed cuff (a bare sleeve-to-wrist diameter step instead), no ribbed waist hem, no back yoke seam. Without the waistband it flares into a labcoat cone rather than the drawn cropped bomber. The collar and the fold-back front edges DO read, and the shoes and rolled jean cuffs are genuinely well constructed.
At 40px the round glasses -- his only memorable mark -- go sub-pixel and he becomes a generic brown-jacket kid. 3.9 is weak.

NOT findings, checked and cleared so they are not re-raised: nothing is severed (neck, wrists, ankles continuous); legs are not fused, 3.12 passes in bind, A-pose and run and the +14.5 ankle-daylight delta is the concept's legs-together drawing per 6b.4; ears are properly constructed with rim, inner shadow and lobe (3.10); a real nose breaks the profile silhouette; the shoe 'grey vs cream' question is instrument geometry, all three shoe metrics measure ok; all four expression stills are genuinely painted and distinct; the profile's near-side eye absence is partly the expected 90-degree foreshortening, though here it is total occlusion by hair rather than foreshortening; the glasses ring standing proud of the cheek in profile is a receding-brow geometry artefact, not floating accessory geometry.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The body silhouette is right - bomber, cuffed jeans, low-tops all read with colour stripped. The cap is not. In profile the crown is a smooth hemisphere and the brim is a constant-thickness rectangular plank with a square tip, butt-joined at a hard corner; the sheet draws a six-panel dome with a button and seam arcs, and a thick tapering shelf whose sides roll down. From the front the brim collapses to an 8px strip on a ~160px head (5%) against the sheet's 22-33px on a 196px head (11-17%), so the front silhouette reads as a bowl hat with a rim, not a ballcap. Butt-jointed primitives are explicitly what 3.1 caps, and this is the clearest case on the board. 3, not 4, because the cap IS the character and its large read is wrong from the front.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Measured, not eyeballed: head height 32.3% of figure against the concept's 33.1% (-0.82, ok) and head width:height 0.89 against 0.93 (-0.04, ok) - both inside tolerance, so 3.13 holds and this is the concept's head, not the proxy's. Joints read as connected forms: the shoulder stays a rounded deltoid where the arm drops in the A-pose, the elbow line is continuous through run and swing_contact, knees do not pinch. Neck-into-jacket is a plain cylinder junction and the torso is a single tapered tube rather than the sheet's slight chest/waist break, which is what keeps it off a 5.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: measure:strands: concept 4.49 minima/row at mean prominence 16.7 over 88 rows; delivered 1.59 at 23.8 over 73 rows - 35% of the concept's strand count at 143% of its prominence. That is up from the 20% recorded for him in the roster sweep and well clear of the 15% line the instrument's header marks as the point where the number stops being the target; band is upper-middle of the roster's 2-57% spread. Front board shows a genuinely designed hairline - scalloped fringe across the forehead with temple lobes falling over the ears - and no bare-skull read at any board or runtime angle. The profile is where it stops: one smooth featureless mass with a hard stepped cut at the sideburn. Grouping on one view, blob on the other, so 4.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Real construction is present and I checked the builder before saying anything was missing: the navy ribbed cuff reads as a distinct band at the wrist, the jeans carry a rolled light-blue cuff, the shoes have a two-tone cupsole, a toe bumper and lace strokes (shoe band metrics all in tolerance - dominant tone 65.1 vs 69.7, second 26.9 vs 28.4, saturation 23.5 vs 22.3). But the jacket's loudest sheet details do not survive. The collar rib is authored at z 2.575/2.600 yet reads on the board only as two black wedges at the shoulder tops - there is no band across the front of the neck. The hem rib is a hairline where the sheet makes it the jacket's strongest horizontal. Grepping sculpt-ace-source.py for 'zip' and 'pocket' returns nothing: the front zipper with its pull and the welt pockets, both prominent on all five sheet views, are genuinely not built. And at 12x the tee's top edge against the neck is a 1-2px sawtooth. Colour boundaries themselves are constructed - jacket/tee, cuff, jean roll and sole splits all land on geometry rings with a 1-2px ramp, not painted gradients.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: All four runtime stills are genuinely painted - 281551 / 279190 / 279775 / 278822 bytes, within 1% of each other and nowhere near the ~82k empty-cell signature (dazzle-grin 82133, sprout-grin 82053 on the same board). grin opens on a tooth row, tongue opens on teeth plus a pink tongue, angry drives the brows down and in over an open frown, cheer opens wide - every one legible at draft-card distance, so 3.14 is clean. The nose is a real form (nose_push in the sculpt) and it breaks the profile silhouette; no decal-island seam anywhere on the head, and the face survives the run and swing clips. Held to 4 by the eyebrows, which are hard-edged flat quadrilaterals against the sheet's tapered brows, and by a nose that all but disappears in the front board render - a soft shadow where the sheet has a defined tip and nostrils.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Hero is fine: the review page reports 'model model', the idle and run stills read as a specific kid in a blue cap and bomber, and the cap silhouette does work at hero from three-quarter. The 40px strip is where it fails. Ace's one memorable read is supposed to be the ballcap, and at 40px the brim - 5% of head height from the front - vanishes entirely, leaving a blue blob over a blue-and-cream torso that is not separable from the roster's other cap kids. The 40px read has to carry the brim or it carries nothing distinctive, so 3.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: THE SEVERANCE IS A TRUE BREAK, NOT A NEAR-MISS AT A THIN WAIST. I re-scanned both bind-pose boards myself: row y=421 (60.6% from crown, 39.4% height) carries ZERO figure pixels across the entire body in rocket-rosa-front-review.png and rocket-rosa-profile-review.png. It is not a pinch — y=420 is the cream shirt hem spanning x224-315 (92px, one of the WIDEST points on the figure) and y=422 is the shorts spanning x217-322; 100% of that width vanishes for one row. Sampled alpha at y421 x230/250/270/290 = 2,4,4,4 (front) and 0,11,17,10 (profile): effectively transparent, ~2% coverage, real background. The A-pose boards report 'no empty rows' ONLY because the dropped arms bridge that scanline (front-apose y421 = [[165,185],[354,374]] — arm spans only, torso still gone). Cropped at 8x it is unmistakable: a clean horizontal slit of backdrop running the full hip width between the shirt slab and the shorts. It is masked at runtime by the toon ink outline, so it is a board/3.7 failure rather than a live-render one — but 3.7 is a board check and it fails. SECOND, INDEPENDENT HOLE at the same junction: y422-435 has a 6px see-through notch at x267-272 between the two shorts side-boxes, above the separate centre gusset — you see backdrop through the shorts crotch for 14 rows. Beyond the holes, the large read misses the turnaround: from the FRONT the character is a centred top-knot bun, not the sheet's high side ponytail; from BEHIND (swing_contact, the batting camera's own angle) cap and tail merge into one undifferentiated soft-serve cone with no tail read at all; in PROFILE the tail is a flat faceted sail with a hard spike at the top-back and a sharp V-chip where the crest tube butt-joins the fan (cropped at 12x — a construction corner, not a hair groove). And the stance is wrong: my own measure:fidelity run gives ankle daylight 54.2 delivered vs 0.00 concept, +54.2 against a tolerance of 12 — a wide splayed A where the sheet stands narrow.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The measurable half is genuinely good and I will not punish it: my own measure:fidelity run gives head height 36.5% of figure vs the concept's 36.5% (delta +0.02) and head width:height 0.67 vs 0.69 (delta -0.02), both comfortably inside tolerance, so 3.13's face-aspect check passes and the child proportion is the turnaround's, not the proxy's. What fails is the second clause of 3.2 — 'joints read as connected forms'. The hip joint is not merely unconvincing, it is absent (see the y=421 finding). The shorts are three butt-joined boxes, a left panel, a right panel and a narrower centre gusset that sits lower and steps forward with hard ink-outlined seams down both sides; at the runtime hero camera it reads as a nappy flap, not a crotch. The sleeve hem to bare forearm is a hard step with no deltoid: the sleeve is a box and a thin tube emerges from it, so at idle and run the shoulder never rounds. In swing_contact the lead elbow reads as two cylinders meeting at a kink rather than a continuous elbow line (3.11 concern). Sock cuff to calf is a crisp constructed step, which is correct. So: proportions right, connections wrong.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured by me, and tightening the band makes it WORSE, not better, so the default is not flattering it. Default band 5-45% of head height: delivered 0.99 strand minima/row, prominence 61.1 (81 rows) vs concept 6.16 and 19.6 (85 rows) = 16% of the concept's strand count at 312% of its prominence. I re-ran at 5-30%, which is pure crown well above the hairline (delivered brows sit at ~46% of head height, so the default does graze them): 0.53 vs 5.50 minima/row = 10% of concept count at 171% prominence. Honest number: 10-16%, i.e. a smooth faceted blob with a handful of very deep facet creases and no strand grouping whatever. Rubric 3.3 caps a featureless blob at 4; this one cannot reach 4 because the silhouette half fails too. (a) The signature is a HIGH SIDE PONYTAIL and from the front it is a centred top-knot: a hexagonal prism butt-joined to a dome with a visible ledge ring at the join. (b) From behind, cap and tail are one mass, so at the batting camera the ponytail does not exist. (c) HAIR SWALLOWS THE FACE. The turnaround keeps a full forehead of roughly one eye-height between brow and hairline; the delivered hairline is a hard horizontal edge sitting directly ON the eyebrows, and in rocket-rosa-runtime-face-angry.png the raised inner brow is partly overlapped by the hair mass. There is no forehead on this kid at any angle. (d) The profile crown is one flat polygon plane with hard unsmoothed facet boundaries.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely mixed, and the shoes are the best thing on the asset. Cropped at 8x, each sneaker has a cream midsole with a distinct darker outsole strip under it, a navy upper, a cream toe cap, three crisp cream stripes and a dark lace stroke — that is a constructed shoe, not a primitive volume, and my measure:fidelity run confirms the colour split is right (shoe dominant tone 67.4 vs concept 70.0, second tone 32.6 vs 28.6, band saturation 16.1 vs 19.7, all ok). The collar piping and sleeve piping are crisp loft-ring edges, not smears, and the sock cuff is a hard constructed edge. AGAINST that: the shorts are the worst-constructed garment on any board I have looked at — three butt-joined boxes with a see-through notch above the centre gusset, no waistband, no hem roll, and a gusset panel that reads at hero scale as a separate rectangular flap. The tee is a hard-cornered slab with a flat disc bottom and no hem at all, and it does not reach the shorts. ON THE PAINTED-VS-CONSTRUCTED QUESTION: mostly constructed edges (piping, stripes, sock cuff, shirt/shorts volumes are separate lofts), but two are painted gradients — the shoe's cream toe cap blends into the navy through a soft mottled blur with a raised bubble artefact in the middle of the cream, and the midsole/upper boundary is equally cloudy. The lace is a painted stroke, not geometry. TEAM_MASK EXTENT (judging extent, not colour, per the brief): the scrunchie is a ~40x8px orange sliver on the tail in the profile board plus a detached 3-4px orange island beside it, invisible from the front and invisible at 40px in all three views. That is too little accent surface for either team palette to read in game (2.4).

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The four runtime-face stills are the asset's real strength and I checked them for the empty-file trap first: grin 285439, cheer 283363, tongue 283495, angry 283961 bytes — all within 1% of each other, none near the ~29% tell, and all four are visually distinct when cropped and tiled. 3.14 passes cleanly and is not close: grin is a closed smile with a teeth band, cheer opens to an upper teeth row over a dark red interior, tongue shows a real pink tongue below the teeth, angry is a down-turned frown with a modelled lower lip and inward-angled brows. That reads at draft-card distance. My measure:fidelity run also clears 6b.3: visible face left 49.3% vs concept 43.8%, right 47.9% vs 44.4%, asymmetry 1.43 — all ok, and 3.13's aspect ratio passes (0.67 vs 0.69). The nose is NOT absent — nose_push is in the sculpt script and the profile crop confirms geometry breaking the silhouette — but it breaks it as a sharp beak point rather than the sheet's soft button, and under the board's flat front light it produces no shading break at all, so the front board view reads as a noseless face. The near-side eye reading as a foreshortened grey sliver in the profile is EXPECTED at a true 90-degree ortho and I am not counting it. What holds this to 3 is 3.5's own 5-clause and the hero evidence: cropped at 6x from rocket-rosa-runtime-hero.png there is a hard, ink-outlined, dotted decal-island seam running down the face from the brow through the cheek where the flat face plane meets the skull, catching visibly different light on each side. 3.5 bars exactly that. Add the swallowed forehead, flat parallelogram brows and a skull with no cheekbone, jaw or chin plane, and the face is a sticker on an egg that happens to animate well.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Split result. The hero 3/4 (rocket-rosa-runtime-hero.png) reads well — the ponytail is clearly a ponytail, the face lands, the white/navy/orange colours all separate against grass and dirt, the review page reports 'model model' (4.1 satisfied) at 27.7k tris, and run reads as a genuinely energetic sprint with clear daylight between the legs. I built my own 40px strip from the hero, front board and profile board and upscaled it: from PROFILE and 3/4 the tail mass survives and she reads as a girl with hair. From the FRONT she does not. At 40px front-on the top-knot collapses to an unreadable nub, the ears become the dominant shape, and she reads as a short-haired boy in a white tee — the same read as half the roster, with zero trace of the one thing that makes her Rocket. No orange is visible at 40px in any of the three views. Since the draft card portrait and the pitcher's on-screen presentation are both front-facing, that is a real 3.6/3.9 miss, not a technicality. One more motion note: the ponytail hangs dead vertical through the whole run cycle with no trail or whip, which for the character literally named Rocket is a wasted signature.

Worse, the 4-vs-5 discriminator (butt-joined primitives) fails outright at the shoulder: at 5x-8x the T-pose sleeve is a plain cylinder butt-joined to the torso with a hard vertical seam and a 32px-wide wedge of true background between sleeve and torso (front-review y311-312, confirmed by alpha scan and by an 8x crop of x180-360/y268-328), and the collar is a jagged sawtooth rather than a band. headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The size relationships pass by measurement (head height 30.4% of figure vs 31.0%, delta -0.62, ok; head width:height +0.01, ok). The criterion's other half — 'joints read as connected forms' — fails hard. The neck is a long exposed cylinder; the concept sets the head almost directly on the shoulders. The arm is a uniform noodle from shoulder to wrist with no deltoid ball, no elbow swell and a small flat paddle hand, against the sheet's chunky toddler forearm. The shoulder is not a form at all: it is a butt joint plus a sheared triangular flap. I read the sculpt script and the cause is in code, not in the eye — ARM_STATIONS carries rings at x=0.335 and x=0.400 (ARM_SHOULDER_X), SHOULDER_BLEND has keys {0.215, 0.300, 0.345, 0.420}, and sculptlib/arm.py:130 does `spec.shoulder_blend.get(round(x, 3))` — an exact-key lookup that returns None for 0.335 and 0.400, so both rings weight 100% to the Arm bone, while the 0.345 and 0.420 entries match no station and never fire. Two of four blend entries are dead and the two rings closest to the joint are unblended. This is the recorded ARM SHOULDER_BLEND lesson reproduced verbatim.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: DECAPITATED. I re-measured every board view myself: figure spans rows 73-647 (h=575px = 4.0ft) and rows 261-265 contain ZERO figure pixels in cricket-front-review, profile-review, front-apose-review and profile-apose-review alike — 5 rows, 0.035ft, at 32.7% of figure height. Row counts run 54,50,44,40,34,28,22,10,0,0,0,0,0,40,42,40 (front): the jaw tapers to a point, five rows of pure background, then the torso starts at a constant 40px. I cropped rows 215-295 at 6x with a magenta backdrop and the background is visibly straight through: the head FLOATS above a flat-topped neck stub. Root cause found in the sculpt source and it is arithmetic, not a posing artifact — HEAD_CENTER z 3.220 with HEAD_RADII z 0.460 puts the skull's bottom pole at z 2.760, while NECK_LEVELS tops out at z 2.720. 0.040ft of the boy has no geometry. Rubric 3.7 forbids holes and gaps outright and this is the worst shape on that list; silhouette.lint cannot see it because a gap open at both sides is never an enclosed pocket. Beyond the severance the large read still misses the sheet: the concept's profile is a radiating spiked mop over a clear cheek, jaw and ear, while the delivered profile is a smooth motorcycle-helmet shell with a hard flat-cut vertical back plane and an angular bevelled corner (a butt-joined primitive, which 3.1's 5/5 explicitly excludes), the torso is one bell-shaped apron slab from chest to hip ending in a hard hem ledge, and the sleeve meets the bare forearm at a visible diameter step with no transition. The one metric measure:fidelity puts outside tolerance is silhouette too: daylight between the ankles 26.7 delivered vs 0.00 concept (tol 12) — the bind stance is planted far wider than the sheet's feet-together stand. LEGS ARE NOT FUSED (3.12 is fine: clear daylight between thighs and calves in bind, A-pose and the run still) — if anything they are too far apart.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The RATIOS are fine and I took them myself with measure:fidelity: head height 32.7% of figure vs the concept's 34.2% (delta -1.48, ok) and head width:height 0.93 vs 0.87 (delta +0.05, ok), so 3.13's aspect check passes and this is not a bobblehead. What fails is the other half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms.' The head is not connected to the body AT ALL (see 3.1: 0.040ft of missing geometry between skull pole z 2.760 and neck top z 2.720), which is the most extreme possible failure of a joint reading as a connected form. It is not an isolated slip either: in the A-pose front board the shoulder is a square-cornered block with no deltoid — the tee sleeve is a fat cylinder that simply stops, and the bare forearm emerges from it a full step narrower with a visible flat ring at the junction. The hand is a paddle mitt. The neck itself is a bare flat-topped cylinder butt-joined to a flat-cut head underside, with no sternocleidomastoid, no trapezius sweep and no jaw shadow to bed it in. Ratios that measure correct on a figure that comes apart at the neck cannot score 4.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I ran measure:strands myself at three bands, and the default 5-45% is not the culprit — the result is the same everywhere. 5-45%: concept 10.19 strand minima/row at prominence 24.4 over 98 rows, delivered 3.19 at prominence 72.2 over 70 rows = 31% of the concept's strand count at 296% of its prominence. Tightening to 5-30% to stay off the forehead and brows (where skin/hair and brow edges could count as false creases) gives concept 8.98 vs delivered 3.59 = 40% at 278%; 5-35% gives 9.34 vs 3.75 = 40% at 295%. The band choice moves the number by nine points and the verdict not at all. That count/prominence signature is diagnostic: the delivered mass has almost no creases, and the few it has are enormous — they are the facets of an 18-gon and the bases of the spike cones, not strands. I confirmed the mechanism in the sculpt source rather than inferring it: ring_loft_cap builds `segments = 18` columns and modulates them with `clump = 1.0 + 0.055 * cos(6 * theta)` — six lobes across eighteen columns is 3.0 columns per lobe, below the ~4 a crease needs to read, and the amplitude is 5.5% of half-width. That clump can never produce a groove; the code's own comment says it exists so 'the mop's back is not a featureless helmet,' and the board shows it failed at exactly that. What ships is a smooth glossy bowl with fourteen discrete cone spikes stuck on the crown, which reads as horns, not hair. Rubric 3.3 caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 'however correct its silhouette' — and this silhouette is NOT correct either. The concept mop radiates pointed locks in every direction, all round the sides and back; the delivered mass is a bare rounded shell everywhere except the crown mohawk. THE HAIR ALSO SWALLOWS FACE THE SHEET KEEPS CLEAR: CAP_FRINGE drops the lower edge to z 3.000 at |x| 0.44, and the profile crop shows two claw-shaped hair lobes hanging over the cheekbone down to mouth level with the near ear buried and the eye reduced to a sliver, where the sheet's profile keeps the whole eye, cheek, jaw and a fully drawn ear clear. I also cropped the profile hair at 12x around the temple and there is a genuine 4-5px dark pinhole notch in the otherwise unbroken shell.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The most defensible category, and it still does not reach 4. Real construction IS present and I verified it by cropping rather than asserting: the shoes carry a cream cupsole band, a toe cap, a lit collar and two-to-three lace stripes; there is a ringer collar at the neck; the ankle carries a rolled cuff ring; the bib carries a pocket badge. Measured shoe split is honest too — measure:fidelity reads the concept's shoe tones as #fbeedc and #7b644b and reports dominant 49.8 vs 54.9, second 50.2 vs 44.0, saturation 24.5 vs 27.4, all inside tolerance. But the PRIMARY garment is a primitive. Cropping the torso at 4x, the overalls read as a single bell-shaped apron flaring from the chest and terminating in a hard horizontal hem ledge at the hip — no side seam, no leg-opening construction, and the two straps are flat plates butt-joined onto a flat bib with no buckle, no button and no topstitch, where the concept shows brass buttons on both straps, a bib pocket with a lip and a hip patch pocket. The team-accent badge (TEAM_MASK, raw grey on the board, so I judge EXTENT not colour) is proportionate and correctly confined to the bib pocket — that part is right — but it is a flat rectangle with no pocket lip, so it reads as a sticker. In profile the shoe is a bar of soap: a rounded rectangular loaf with no heel counter, no tongue, no toe upturn and a flat untreaded sole. Two fidelity misses I checked against a 4x crop of the concept's feet: the concept's rolled cuff is clearly light DENIM with orange topstitching, while CUFF is authored #D5CDBE and renders near-cream; and the concept ankle is BARE SKIN between cuff and shoe, while the delivered adds a prominent white tube-sock column that is not in the sheet at all.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Genuinely mixed, and it lands at 3. The strengths are real: the eyes are the best-sculpted thing on the model, with a proper iris, pupil, highlight and lash line that read at hero scale; the freckles are present and placed as the sheet places them; and 3.14 passes cleanly. I checked all four -runtime-face-*.png stills and they are ALL genuinely painted, not stubs — bytes 275741 / 273942 / 274270 / 273929 for grin / cheer / tongue / angry, within 0.7% of each other, nowhere near the ~29% signature of an empty one — and I cropped and composited the four faces at 4x: grin is a closed curved smile, cheer opens to a red mouth interior with teeth, tongue puts a pink tongue out over the lower lip, angry drops the corners and angles the brows. Four distinct, readable emotions with lips, teeth and tongue, none collapsing to a stroke. The failures are structural. At 9x the face is unmistakably a DECAL ISLAND: a hard-edged, stair-stepped skin-tone patch pasted onto the skull, with the boundary visible as right-angle staircases across the forehead and down the right cheek and a tonal step between the decal skin and the sculpted skin below it. Rubric 3.5 names 'no visible decal-island seam' as a 5/5 requirement, and this is the seam the clause is about. The brows are flat dark quadrilaterals, not brow forms. And the nose does not read: nose_push IS authored (an upturned button, max 0.086 push at |nx|<0.18 around nz -0.44 — I grepped it rather than calling it absent), but at board scale the front view shows only the faintest shading between the eyes where the concept has a distinct round button nose with nostrils. 3.5's 5/5 asks for 'a real nose that breaks the profile' and 'a form, not a sticker'; this is a sticker with an invisible nose.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The review page reports 'model model', so 4.1 is satisfied and this is fidelity evidence, not proxy evidence. At hero scale the character reads: the expressions land, the eyes carry, the palette (brown mop, green tee, blue overalls, taupe canvas shoes) is legibly Cricket, and the run and swing_contact stills show two clear legs, a bent elbow and planted feet with no visible tearing. I cropped the runtime hero head at 6x and the neck DOES read as connected once the skinning closes it, so the severance is a board defect rather than a gameplay one — but 3.7 is a board check and the board is the delivered evidence. At the board's 40-pixel strip the read degrades to 'brown bowl, green top, blue bottom.' The one memorable thing about this kid on the sheet is a wild spiked mop radiating in every direction, and the delivered bowl-with-a-crown-mohawk keeps only a fuzzy crown fringe of that at 40px — the sides and back go smooth and the read becomes generic against a roster of brown-haired boys. Add the sticker seam and the fringe overhang, both visible at hero scale, and this cannot be called 4.

The nose does not read in the front board view. nose_push is authored (max 0.086 tip push) but produces only faint shading where the concept shows a distinct round button nose with nostrils.
Eyebrows are flat dark quadrilaterals with cut corners, not tapered brow forms.
The neutral mouth collapses to a single thin stroke on the board. (The four expression stills are fine — 3.14 passes — but the default face is the one on the draft card.)
Shoulders are square blocks with no deltoid, and the tee sleeve meets the bare forearm at a hard diameter step with a visible flat ring — most obvious in cricket-front-apose-review.

The overalls are one bell-shaped apron slab from chest to hip with a hard hem ledge — no side seams, no leg-opening construction, no strap buttons or buckles, and no hip pocket, where the concept shows brass buttons on both straps and a patch pocket.
The bib pocket badge is correctly confined and correctly sized as the team accent (extent judged, colour ignored), but it is a flat rectangle with no pocket lip, so it reads as a decal.
The rolled ankle cuff is authored cream (CUFF #D5CDBE) where the concept's roll is light DENIM with orange topstitching — confirmed against a 4x crop of the concept's feet.
The delivered model adds prominent white tube socks between cuff and shoe; the concept shows bare skin at the ankle.

In profile the shoe is a soap-bar loaf: no heel counter, no tongue, no toe upturn, flat untreaded sole. The front view's lace stripes and cupsole are good and should be carried into the profile forms.
Two thin black hook-shaped slivers sit low on the front of both shoes (symmetric, so geometry rather than noise) and read as scratches at hero scale.

Bind stance is too wide: ankle daylight 26.7 against the concept's 0.00 (tol 12) — the only metric measure:fidelity flags. Read it as a stance note, not a tolerance to widen: the sheet stands feet together.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The FRONT large-read is fine: top-knot, A-line dress, bare legs, cream sock cuffs — recognisable with colour stripped. The PROFILE is not. Cropping peaches-profile-review.png at 190,120 (110x130 @8x) shows (a) the temple wisp as a flat brown PLANK with a hard rectangular cut end, floating over the cheek and interpenetrating it, (b) no nose worth the name — the front-of-face silhouette from brow to lip is a single soft curve broken only by a ~4px tan wedge, (c) an oversized curled ear shell occupying roughly the front third of the head's side, notched by hair. Worse, rubric 3.1's 5-criterion ('transitions organic, not butt-joined primitives') fails at the shoulder: peaches-front-apose-review.png cropped at 200,250 (60x60 @12x) shows the deltoid dome as a DISCRETE ELLIPSOID stacked on the arm cylinder, with a hard silhouette step where it overhangs the arm and a dark crease under it. It is a ball butt-joined to a tube, not a fairing. Also the bodice is a plain truncated cone — the concept's scoop neck, shoulder straps and armscye are all absent, replaced by one cream ring around a tube. Nothing is SEVERED; the white seen at the armpit is background between limb and torso, not a mesh hole. 2.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The numbers are green and I took them: head height 29.6% of figure vs the concept's 30.4% (-0.80, ok); head width:height 0.84 vs 0.80 (+0.04, ok); face visible left 30.0 vs 26.8 and right 32.9 vs 32.7, asymmetry 2.86 — all ok. No bobblehead. What fails the category's second clause — 'joints read as connected forms' — is everything below the neck. The neck is a long unmodulated skin cylinder (a stalk; peaches-front-apose-review.png at 6x, 170,220) with the head sitting on it rather than growing from it. The shoulder is the separate ball described above. The leg from hem to sock is a straight untapered pipe with no knee, no calf swell and no ankle taper — visible in the same A-pose crop and in the 8x foot crop. Measured daylight between the ankles reads 34.0 against the concept's 0.00 (tol 12): per 6b.4 that is a STANCE finding, not a tolerance to widen — the bind pose plants her a third of a leg-width wider than the sheet's feet-together standing pose, which is why she reads bandy rather than as the concept's neat little girl. 3.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Measured myself, and it is the roster's worst reading so far. npm run measure:strands -- peaches at the DEFAULT band (5-45% of head height): concept 8.71 strand minima/row at prominence 20.5 over 86 rows; delivered 0.10 minima/row at prominence 43.7 over 67 rows — 1% of the concept's strand count at 213% of its prominence. I re-ran at 5-30% (concept 8.85, delivered 0.12 = 1%, 253% prominence) and 10-40% (concept 9.40, delivered 0.10 = 1%, 251%) specifically to lift the band clear of the forehead/brow edges the tool's header warns about. All three bands agree: essentially ZERO strand grouping. And the eye confirms the ruler — the bun is a smooth acorn dome with a pointed apex and a hard STEP SEAM ring where it lands on the cap, over a smooth featureless helmet. The concept's bun is a visibly twisted, coiled braid. Rubric 3.3 caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 however correct its silhouette; this is below that because the silhouette is also wrong (acorn vs coil) and because the mass misbehaves at the edges: the two temple wisps are plain tapered tubes (builder.tube radii 0.050/0.062/0.024) that in the FRONT board and in all four runtime face stills lie directly ACROSS the ear ellipse on both sides — the known 'wisps over the ears' regression is visibly back in the delivered render even though the script comment claims they sit in front of it — and in peaches-runtime-hero.png the near wisp crosses the near EYE. No bare-skull read, which is the one thing that keeps this off 1. 2.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Split verdict, and the split lands at 3. Constructed and reading: the scalloped six-petal hem shell with its cream edge lip (build_petal_hem, three loft rows with a cos(6*theta) scallop) is genuinely a hem and reads as one in the swing still; the cream waistband and neckline are real loft rings with their own vertex colours, not painted gradients — I checked the builder, every garment colour boundary here is a CONSTRUCTED EDGE (TORSO_LEVELS via dress_color, the petal specs, and LEG_STATIONS for the sock), no gradient fakes. The shoe has a real cupsole, toe cap and lace geometry (ShoeSpec/build_shoe), visible at 6x. Not constructed: the bodice has NO straps, NO scoop neck and NO armhole — the concept draws all three clearly from front and back, and the delivered garment is a cone with one cream band around its top, so the sleeveless read comes from the arm leaving the cone rather than from a cut garment. The leaf appliqué is a single smooth TRIM ellipsoid (0.070, 0.022, 0.120) — a featureless teardrop blob, where the sheet draws a large outlined leaf with a central vein running most of the skirt panel. And the shoe is measurably off: the band's second tone reads 63.0% against the concept's 47.5% (+15.5, tol 8) and the band's mean saturation 27.4 against 32.7 (-5.31, tol 4) — the cream cupsole has eaten the peach canvas, so the sneaker reads greyish-white rather than the sheet's peach. TEAM_MASK extent is correctly small and declared: two leg loft stations (z 0.425 and 0.390) forming a sock band; I judged extent only, not the raw grey. 3.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The single worst thing on this character, and it is not subtle. Crop peaches-runtime-face-grin.png at 460,140 (150x150 @6x), or peaches-front-review.png at 190,60 (160x200 @5x): a lighter, flat-shaded polygonal DECAL ISLAND covers the forehead and eye region with hard STRAIGHT-EDGED seams — a visible staircase step across the upper-left forehead, a squared notch at the upper right, and a vertical drop at the right temple that CLIPS the right eyebrow off in a straight cut. Rubric 3.5 names 'no visible decal-island seam' explicitly; this is the seam, and it is legible at hero scale in every one of the four runtime stills, not only in a 6x crop. There is also no nose as a FORM — the front view has only a faint soft shading lozenge and the profile a ~4px wedge, so the face is a sticker on an ellipsoid, which 3.5 calls out by name. In peaches-runtime-hero.png (crop 460,150 @7x) the 3/4 hero read is worse still: hair covers the far half of the head, the near temple wisp crosses the near eye, and only one eye is partly legible. What passes: all four -runtime-face-*.png stills are GENUINELY PAINTED — I took the byte sizes myself (grin 280,847 / cheer 279,876 / tongue 279,836 / angry 279,780, a 0.4% spread, none anywhere near the ~29% stub size), and grin shows a toothed crescent, tongue an open mouth with a red tongue, so 3.14's mouth-emotion check holds. No freckles and no blush anywhere, both of which the sheet carries and the record listed as polish. 2.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: Two different answers. At 40 px the board's zoom strip still delivers the one memorable read — brown top-knot over a marigold A-line — so 3.9 passes; the silhouette is distinctive enough among the roster that the bun survives to 1-2 px of value contrast. At HERO the read degrades: the face is half-occluded by hair and the crossing wisp, and the deltoid ball becomes a separate object because the toon shader gives it its OWN closed ink outline — crop peaches-runtime-run.png at 490,320 (130x130 @7x) and the far shoulder is an outlined sphere sitting beside the neck, the near arm is outlined away from the torso along its whole root. Colour holds at runtime (the dress is properly marigold in peaches-runtime-hero.png) even though the fidelity board washes it out: I sampled the board's dress at #d5b07f, saturation 0.406, against the concept's #e2932d at 0.799, and the board's cheek at 0.387 against the concept's 0.717 — that is the board's key light, not a vertex-colour slip, so I am not scoring it. Field scale is fine, hero scale is not. 3.

polishFindings: 3.5 BLOCKER — visible decal-island seam on the face. A lighter, flat-shaded polygonal patch covers the forehead and eye region with hard straight edges: a staircase step across the upper-left forehead, a squared notch upper-right, and a vertical seam at the right temple that clips the right eyebrow off in a straight cut. Cropped and confirmed at 5x in peaches-front-review.png (190,60 160x200) and at 6x in all four peaches-runtime-face-*.png (460,140 150x150). Legible at 1x, not only at zoom.

3.11 BLOCKER — the deltoid dome exists in the script but does not fair. Cropped at 12x from peaches-front-apose-review.png (200,250 60x60): the skin ellipsoid reads as a discrete ball stacked on the arm cylinder, overhanging it with a hard silhouette step and a dark crease underneath. At runtime the toon shader draws it its OWN closed ink outline — peaches-runtime-run.png at 7x (490,320) shows the far shoulder as an outlined sphere beside the neck. Four ring/cap/blend rounds were replaced by a dome that has the same failure mode one primitive up.

3.8 — the temple wisps still cross the ears in the delivered render. In peaches-front-review.png at 12x (285,155 60x60) and in every runtime face still, the brown wisp tube lies directly across the tan ear ellipse on both sides. The script comment asserts they sit IN FRONT of the ears, but in the front orthographic projection wisp x 0.330-0.385 overlays the ear at the skull surface. In profile the same wisp is a flat plank with a hard rectangular cut end floating over and into the cheek.

3.3 — the bun is an acorn, not a coil. measure:strands returns 1% of the concept's strand count at all three bands I ran. There is also a hard STEP SEAM ring where the bun's base lands on the cap (visible at 5x in front and profile, and at 7x in the hero), so the two hair volumes read as two objects rather than one designed mass.

3.4 — the dress bodice has no straps, no scoop neck and no armhole. The concept draws all three from front and back; the delivered garment is a truncated cone with a single cream ring around its top, so the sleeveless read comes only from the arm leaving the cone.

3.4 — the leaf appliqué is a smooth featureless TRIM ellipsoid (radii 0.070, 0.022, 0.120), a teardrop blob with no outline and no central vein, where the sheet draws a large veined leaf across most of the skirt's lower panel. It is also noticeably smaller relative to the skirt than the sheet's.

6b.2 — the sneaker reads greyish-cream, not peach. Second tone 63.0% of the band vs the concept's 47.5% (+15.5, tol 8) and mean saturation 27.4 vs 32.7 (-5.31, tol 4): the cream cupsole and toe bumper have eaten the peach canvas upper. The lace geometry survives but at 6x (peaches-front-review.png 180,560 190x120) it reads as three hairline scratches plus a black eyelet wedge rather than laces.

6b.4 — stance, not tolerance. Ankle daylight measures 34.0 against the concept's 0.00 (tol 12). Do not widen the tolerance; the bind pose stands her a third of a leg-width wider than the sheet's feet-together standing pose.

3.2 — the neck is a long unmodulated skin cylinder and the leg from hem to sock is a straight untapered pipe with no knee, no calf swell and no ankle taper. Both read as primitives the garments happen to end on.

Minor artifact, cropped before reporting — a faint dashed trail of ~4 dark olive pixels runs inboard from the armpit onto the dress in peaches-runtime-swing.png. Cropped at 20x (540,355 45x45): it is an outline fragment where the arm root ring grazes the dress surface, not a hole and not a gouge. Reads as specks of dirt at 1x.
Polish still outstanding from the record: no freckles and no blush anywhere on the delivered face, both of which the turnaround carries clearly on the cheeks and nose bridge.

PASSES I verified rather than assumed: nothing is severed (the white at the armpit is background between limb and torso, not a mesh hole); the legs are two legs with clear daylight between thighs and calves in the front board and A-pose (3.12 passes on the board — the 34% ankle number is an overshoot, not a fusion); ears ARE constructed per EarSpec/build_ear and show rim, concha shadow and lobe in profile (3.10); all garment colour boundaries are constructed loft-ring edges, never painted gradients; all four runtime face stills are genuinely painted (0.4% byte spread); head width:height 0.84 vs 0.80 keeps 3.13 green; grin shows teeth and tongue shows a tongue, so 3.14 holds.
Trap-4 note: the dark slit at the near eye in peaches-profile-review.png is the near-side eye foreshortened in a true 90-degree orthographic profile. Not reported as a defect.
Trap-3 note: TEAM_MASK is raw grey on the board by design. Judged by extent only — it is confined to two leg loft stations forming a sock band, which is correctly small and declared.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Two binary board items fail on measured evidence, so this cannot sit at 4. (a) 3.7 hole/gap: in lefty-profile-review.png the character's near lapel is SEVERED from the jacket by a column of alpha==0 (verified pixel-by-pixel, not eyeballed: y=290 x=238-242 all alpha 0; y=288-308, 21 rows, gap 3-6px). The same break shows in the front board at y=280 (2px). A second detached island sits at y=203-207, x=340-349 (a 10px hair spike clear of the mass). (b) 3.12 legs: the bind-pose board has ZERO rows of inter-leg daylight over the whole leg band (y 397-642); the concept's front figure has 105 such rows with a 56px max gap = 8.46% of figure height. The delivered thighs and calves are one fused navy trapezoid separated only by a shading crease. Separately, the concept's large read is 'backwards cap + long ponytail'; the front silhouette carries neither. The brim IS built (grepped: BRIM_REACH=0.660, build_cap's two-surface wedge) and it does project ~20px beyond the crown's rear in profile, but it is a 0.035-unit wafer entering the dome at mid-height (BRIM_Z_TOP 3.575 vs the cap's lower rim at z=3.400), so from the front and from the gameplay 3/4 camera the cap reads as a smooth beige helmet with no brim at all.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The number wins and it is red: head width:height 0.88 delivered vs 0.98 concept, delta -0.10 against tol 0.08. I re-measured it independently off the front board (head box y 90-254 = 164px tall, max head run 146px) and got 0.890 — the tool is right. Rubric 3.13 is explicit that a head sculpted narrower than its concept never reads as the same kid, and that is exactly what happens: the concept's head is a wide near-circle, the delivered is a tall egg. Head height as %% of figure is fine (29.6 vs 28.4, +1.22 ok). Against that, the neck is a long straight column (see the 8x front crop) where the concept gives her a short child neck tucked into a hood collar, which pushes the read older. Joints are otherwise connected — shoulders keep a round deltoid in run and swing, no popped seams — and the legs' fusion is scored under silhouette, not double-counted here.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The weakest category. From the front board and from all four runtime face stills the head is a bare tan skull under a beige dome: the forehead is 100%% bare skin and the only hair is two ~3px yellow slivers at the temples plus a khaki wedge behind the jaw. I grepped before calling anything absent — FRINGE_WISPS exists (five entries, r=0.055) — so the correct finding is 'built but sub-visible': at 8x you can see exactly two gold specks at the cap's edge where the concept has a thick swept blonde fringe crossing the forehead. That failure is corroborated by the AUTO metric: visible face left of centre 34.2%% vs concept 27.6%% (+6.68, tol 6) and right 34.9%% vs 28.6%% (+6.28) — both sides show MORE bare face than the concept precisely because the hair no longer frames it. The mass itself is not one designed form: the pony is a hard-edged flat card with a chopped-flat tip and a straight vertical cut at the shoulder, and at swing_contact (4x crop) it swings across the front of the shoulder while the navy hood ellipsoid punches through it — a 3.8 interpenetration that reads at hero scale. Strand bands, stated: the DEFAULT 5-45%% band is invalid for this kid (head box 90-254 puts rows 98-164 on the CAP DOME; the cap's lower edge is ~y170), so its '8%% of concept strand count' is really a cap-panel measurement — true as far as it goes (the concept cap has six panel seams, a crown button and eyelets; the delivered dome has one smooth surface and a flat badge). At 45-95%%, where lefty's hair actually is, the delivered carries 55%% of the concept's strand count at 203%% of its prominence — few, over-hard divisions, i.e. slabs — but that band crosses the eyes on both images (the detector has no hair mask, it takes every in-figure pixel in the row), so I treat it as indicative only. Credit where due and I checked it rather than assuming: the authored hue separation DOES hold at runtime. Delivered hair hue 42 / sat 41 vs cheek hue 27 / sat 41 is a 15-degree gap, WIDER than the concept's own 32-vs-23; and against the cap (hue 34, sat 14) the 27-point saturation gap keeps them apart. The hue trick is not the problem; the missing fringe and the card construction are.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely constructed in places, and I confirmed each in the sculpt rather than guessing: build_lapels makes the tee window's edges real geometry (tubes, not a painted stripe), the shoe carries a cream cupsole, toe bumper and lace stubs that survive 4x, build_hood puts a real navy drape at the upper back, and a rolled jogger cuff exists in the leg profile. What holds it at 3: (1) the tee window itself is a PAINTED vertex-colour region, and its top boundary is a soft blurry diagonal gradient across the collarbone at 6x — a painted edge doing a collar's job; (2) the jogger cuff is authored CUFF #2E2F36 against near-identical pants, so a 'proud' cuff renders as no cuff at all; (3) the sleeves end at the wrist with no readable ribbed cuff and the jacket has no hem band or collar band; (4) the concept's cream piping seams down the sleeves and chest — a signature of the garment — are not present anywhere; (5) the cap, grep-verified, is CAP colour for both dome and brim with a single TEAM_MASK badge, so the concept's navy adjuster strap across the front and navy under-brim (the two highest-contrast elements that make the cap read as backwards) are unmodelled; (6) the same lapel that earns credit is the piece that floats free of the jacket in profile. TEAM_MASK extent, judged as extent and not colour: one badge-sized panel on the dome front, correctly modest.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The strongest category and a real pass. All four runtime-face stills are genuinely painted, not empty — 276.8/276.9/278.3/277.1 KB, within 0.6%% of each other, and visually distinct at 5x: grin is a closed-lip smile with a tooth band, cheer opens the mouth with teeth and a red interior, tongue puts a real tongue out, angry drops the brows to a hard angle over a frown. 3.14 passes properly — no cell collapses to a stroke, and the emotions separate at draft-card distance. Brows are painted in the atlas and carry most of the acting. Face left/right asymmetry 0.68 is clean. Held at 4, not 5, for two reasons rubric 3.5 names explicitly: there IS a visible decal-island seam — a straight horizontal band runs edge-to-edge across the forehead just under the cap at 8x, and it stays straight while the skull and cap edge curve, so it is the atlas island's boundary and not the cap's shadow; and the nose is a form in profile (it does break the outline) but on the front it is a nearly unshaded bump, so the features sit ON the skull's planes more than they are integrated into them. Note also that trap 4 does not apply here — the near-side eye in the 90-degree profile is foreshortened exactly as predicted, and I am not filing it.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px read is fine — I built it myself off the front board and the orange/cream/navy tri-band with a blonde flank at the head is memorable and holds. The review page reports 'model model' at 26.9k tris, so 4.1 is satisfied and this is model evidence, not proxy evidence. What fails is the other half of 3.6, identity survival at hero and at the gameplay camera. lefty's concept identity is a girl with long blonde hair and a backwards cap; at the runtime camera she reads as a boy in a smooth beige helmet, because the brim is invisible from every forward angle, the fringe is sub-visible, and the pony is hidden behind the head in the hero, run and all four face stills. The one still where the pony is visible (swing_contact) is the one where it crosses the shoulder and the hood punches through it. Run and idle deformation are otherwise clean — feet plant, shoulders stay round, no tearing — so this is an identity failure at scale, not a rig failure.
